zh: 9.1　分布式对象
en: 9.1　Distributed Objects

zh: 前面对马克萨斯图形艺术与造型艺术的风格分析，建立在这样一个观念之上：作品的集合是一种在时空上分散的“种群”。马克萨斯艺术作为整体，可以在宏观上被概念化为一个在时间与空间中的“分布式对象”。就像一套供24人使用、共216件单品的豪华瓷质茶具与餐具，所有马克萨斯艺术品都属于某种“套装”——当然，比起富有的亲戚送给新婚夫妇的瓷餐具套装，这是一个整合得松散得多的套装。一套瓷餐具作为分布式对象（一个拥有许多空间上分离、各有不同微观历史的部分的对象），靠预先设计而成为一套，即靠斯波德、韦奇伍德或其他厂家的设计和制造人员有意使它们相配。另一方面，马克萨斯艺术的全集并不出自任何这样的中央统筹机构，它只是在两个多世纪的过程中，经由马克萨斯人（艺术家与赞助人）与外人（收藏家、学者等）之间的社会关系网络，通过历史的累积（与删减）才得以形成。也许除了从风格学的观点看，马克萨斯艺术作为分布式对象只有一种脆弱的统一性。它无非是马克萨斯一度繁荣的艺术生产与流通系统如今被割裂、被散落的碎屑或蜕余物——就像马克萨斯人的骸骨：他们活着的身体曾承载令19世纪到访该岛者印象深刻的纹身。留存下来的只有博物馆标本、私人手中的珍玩、素描与图纸，以及学术文本，如施泰因的（以及本书）。虽然散落各地、脱离原有语境，马克萨斯艺术仍保有自己内在的完整性——作为一个宏观整体，而非碎片的聚合。每一件作品、每一个母题、每一条线或刻槽都向其他一切言说。仿佛它们彼此之间存在亲属关系，可以被安置在一个共同的谱系之中，正如它们的制作者可以被安置其中一样。最重要的是，马克萨斯艺术的每一个碎片都与其他每一个共鸣，因为每一件都经由一位马克萨斯人的心智而成，也都是为马克萨斯人的心智而作。
en: The discussion of Marquesan graphic/plastic stylistics, just concluded, has been founded on the notion of a ‘corpus' of artworks as a kind of spatiotemporally dispersed ‘population'. Marquesan art, considered as a whole, can be conceptualized, macroscopically, as a ‘distributed object' in time and space. Like the 216 separate items in a 24-place luxury set of china tea and dinnerware, all Marquesan artworks belong to a kind of ‘set', though, of course, a more loosely integrated set than the sets of china which are presented to young couples as wedding presents by rich relatives. A china dinner-set is bound together, as a distributed object (an object having many spatially separated parts with different micro-histories) by prior design, that is, by the intentional actions of the design and manufacturing staff of Spode, or Wedgwood, or whoever. The corpus of Marquesan art, on the other hand, emanates from no such central executive organization, and has come into being only by historical accretion (and deletion) via a network of social relations, among Marquesans (artists and patrons) and outsiders (collectors, scholars, etc.) over the course of more than two centuries. Except, perhaps, from a stylistic point of view, Marquesan art has only a tenuous unity as a distributed object. It consists of no more than the detritus or exuviae of the once flourishing art-production and circulation system of the Marquesas now sundered and scattered, like the bones of the Marquesans whose living bodies bore the tattoos which so impressed visitors to the islands in the nineteenth century. All that remain are museum specimens, curiosities in private hands, sketches and drawings, and scholarly texts, such as Steinen's (and this one). None the less, despite this geographical scattering and contextual transformation Marquesan art retains an inner integrity of its own, as a macroscopic whole rather than as an aggregate of fragments. Each piece, each motif, each line or groove, speaks to every other one. It is as if they bore kinship to one another, and could be positioned within a common genealogy, just as their makers could be. Above all, each fragment of Marquesan art resonates with every other, because each has passed, uniquely, through a Marquesan mind, and each was directed towards a Marquesan mind.

zh: 马克萨斯的心智当然现在是、过去也一直是属于个体施动者的心智，各各不同、彼此有别。我不想暗示马克萨斯艺术是某种“群体心智”或集体意识的产物。但在接下来的各节中，我确实想以应有的谨慎接近这样一个问题：分布式对象的宏观特征（如“马克萨斯艺术全集”）与个体和集体两种意义上的“心智”之间的关系。我的论证的要旨是：我们从内部所知的、作为“意识”的认知过程，与人工制品领域中分布式对象的时空结构——如某一特定艺术家的作品全集（这里以杜尚为例），或某类艺术品在历史中积累起来的整体（如毛利会堂，见下文）——之间存在结构上的同构性。换言之，艺术史的结构展示了一种外在化、集体化的认知过程。
en: Marquesan minds are and always were, of course, minds belonging to individual agents, different and distinct. I do not want to suggest that Marquesan art is the product of a ‘group mind' or collective consciousness. But in the ensuing sections I do want to approach, with due caution, the problem of the relationship between the macroscopic characteristics of distributed objects (such as ‘the corpus of Marquesan art') and ‘the mind' in both the individual and collective sense. The pith of my argument is that there is isomorphy of structure between the cognitive processes we know (from inside) as ‘consciousness' and the spatio-temporal structures of distributed objects in the artefactual realm such as the œuvre of one particular artist (Duchamp provides my example) or the historical corpus of types of artworks (e.g. Maori meeting houses, see below). In other words, the structures of art history demonstrate an externalized and collectivized cognitive process.

zh: 我必须小心地准备我的论证，因为我意识到自己正在穿越危险的地带。让我回到前几章引入的一些观念，以此为出发点，展开这部分的论证。重申一遍，这些观念关乎某种“内在”之物（心智或意识）与某种“外在”之物——作为“分布式对象”的艺术品聚合体，把多样性与时空分散性同内在连贯性结合在一起——之间的结构同构性。
en: I must prepare my argument with care, for I recognize that I am traversing dangerous ground. Let me return to some of the ideas I introduced in earlier chapters, so that these may provide something by way of a stable platform from which to launch the ideas I want to develop now. These ideas, to reiterate, concern the structural isomorphy between something ‘internal' (mind or consciousness) and something 'external'-aggregates of artworks as ‘distributed objects' combining multiplicity and spatio-temporal dispersion with immanent coherence.

zh: “内在”与“外在”的对立在本作前面的章节中已为读者所熟悉——特别是处理赋予偶像以生命的外在主义与内在主义策略的那些章节（7.9–11节）。我希望那场讨论的一个主要结果是：“内”与“外”的对立永远只是相对而非绝对的差别。“心智”（内在的人）与外在的人之间的对立虽然真实，却只是相对的。如果我们试图深入人的内部，我们似乎找到的只是其他的人——丹尼特的小人；而如果我们作为社会学家而非认知心理学家，试图说明人的外在方面，我们会发现任何一个社会个体都是他与其他人建立的关系的总和，这些关系分布于他一生所历的时间和空间（M. Strathern 1988; Gell “Strathernograms” 1998）。我们内在的人格似乎由我们外在之所是的复制构成，正如培尔·金特及其著名洋葱的寓言所暗示的。因此，记住这一点，那么提出如下看法也许就不算太离奇：人在外部及集体层面的形态，是其内部形态的放大版。尤其如果像我将要做的那样，我们不把“人”视为有边界的生物有机体，而是用这个标签指称环境中一切可以从中溯因出能动性或人格的对象和／或事件。
en: The contrast between ‘internal' and ‘external' will be familiar from preceding sections of this work-in particular sections dealing with the externalist and internalist strategies for animating idols. One major upshot of that discussion, I hope, was that the contrast between ‘inner' and ‘outer' is always only a relative rather than absolute difference. The contrast between ‘mind' (the internal person) and the external person, though real, is only relative. If we seek to delve inside the person all we seem to find are other persons-the homunculi of Dennett-and if, as sociologists rather than as cognitive psychologists, we try to give an account of the external aspect of persons, we find that any one social individual is the sum of their relations (distributed over biographical time and space) with other persons (M. Strathern 1988; Gell ‘Strathernograms' 1998). Our inner personhood seems to consist of replications of what we are externally, as suggested in the parable of Peer Gynt and his famous onion. So, bearing this in mind, it may not be so aberrant to suggest that what persons are externally (and collectively) is a kind of enlarged replication of what they are internally. Especially if, as I shall be doing, we consider ‘persons' not as bounded biological organisms, but use this label to apply to all the objects and/or events in the milieu from which agency or personhood can be abducted.

zh: 由此观之，一个人及其心智并不局限于特定的时空坐标，而是由一系列生命史中的事件与事件记忆、以及一类分散的物质对象、痕迹与遗留物构成——这些可以归属于一个人，并且总和起来见证了一段生命历程中的施动与受动；这段生涯确实可能在生物死亡之后很久仍延续自身。因此，人被理解为索引的总和：这些索引在生前与身后见证某一具体个人的生命历程。个人能动性作为对因果环境的干预，生成这些“分布式对象”之一，即“事物存在方式”中一切可以从中溯因出某种特定能动性的物质差异。
en: Seen in this light, a person and a person's mind are not confined to particular spatio-temporal coordinates, but consist of a spread of biographical events and memories of events, and a dispersed category of material objects, traces, and leavings, which can be attributed to a person and which, in aggregate, testify to agency and patienthood during a biographical career which may, indeed, prolong itself long after biological death. The person is thus understood as the sum total of the indexes which testify, in life and subsequently, to the biographical existence of this or that individual. Personal agency, as intervention in the causal milieu, generates one of these ‘distributed objects', that is, all the material differences in ‘the way things are' from which some particular agency can be abducted.

zh: 我承认这种人格观念既含糊又深奥。幸而我的任务不是描述人格本身，而只是抽象出某些主题，把它们应用于比那个观念性“对象”界定得清楚得多的“分布式对象”——那个观念性对象对应于某个特定施动者或人的存在（而非不存在）在其生命史中所造成的一切影响。我心中所想的、见证能动性的相对界定良好的分布式对象，当然是艺术对象的诸范畴。
en: I recognize that this conception of personhood is both vague and abstruse. Fortunately it is not my task to describe personhood as such, but only to abstract certain themes which can be brought to bear on much more clearly demarcated ‘distributed objects' than the notional ‘object' which corresponds to the aggregate biographical effect wrought by the existence (rather than non-existence) of a particular agent or person. The relatively well-defined distributed objects testifying to agency that I have in mind, are, of course, categories of art objects.

zh: 人格在时间与空间中散布的观念，是无数文化制度与实践的组成部分。祖先神龛、坟墓、纪念物、藏骨堂、圣地等等，都关乎经由分布于环境中的索引把人格扩展到生物生命的界限之外。我将详细考察的第一个例子就属于这一范畴：即新爱尔兰北部及一些邻近岛屿生产的、被称为马兰甘的纪念雕刻类型（

，其特征与意义已由苏珊娜·库希勒在一系列文章中加以分析（Kuchler 1985, 1988, 1992）。我突出这些纪念雕刻有一个特殊理由：因为它们尤为清楚地体现了“分布”的观念（对象和／或人在时间与空间中分布），也体现了那个非凡却根本的观念——某物（原型）的形象是该物（作为分布式对象）的部分。这是于尔耶·希尔恩的观念（见上文7.4节），如我们所见可追溯至伊壁鸠鲁与卢克莱修——即可以被感知的物体放出自身的部分——外皮或皮肤或蒸气——扩散到周围环境中，并在知觉过程中被观者纳入。我们将看到，马兰甘的目的是通过展示纪念雕刻来传递祖先的社会效力（社会声望、仪式特权、土地权利等），这些雕刻作为记忆（内化的视觉形象）被纳入后继者之中。
en: The idea of personhood being spread around in time and space is a component of innumerable cultural institutions and practices. Ancestral shrines, tombs, memorials, ossuaries, sacred sites, etc. all have to do with the extension of personhood beyond the confines of biological life via indexes distributed in the milieu. The first example to which I shall devote detailed consideration belongs to this category, namely, the type of memorial carvings produced in northern New Ireland, and some adjoining islands, known as Malangan (

), whose characteristics and significance have been analysed by Suzanne Kuchler in a series of articles (Kuchler 1985, 1988, 1992). I have a particular reason for highlighting these memorial carvings, because they instantiate, particularly clearly, not just the idea of ‘distribution' (the object and/or person being distributed in time and space) but also the extraordinary, yet essential, notion that images of something (a prototype) are parts of that thing (as a distributed object). This is Yrjo Hirn's idea (see above, Sect. 7.4), traceable, as we saw, to Epicurus and Lucretius-the idea that sensible, perceptible objects, give off parts of themselves-rinds or skins or vapours-which diffuse out into the ambience and are incorporated by the onlooker in the process of perception. The purpose of Malangan, as we will see, is the transmission of ancestral social efficacy (social prestige, ritual privileges, land-rights, etc.) through the display of memorial sculptures which are incorporated into successors as memories (internalized visual images).

zh: 9.2　马兰甘
en: 9.2　Malangan

zh: 各收藏机构中约有5,000件被称为马兰甘类型的雕刻，这使它们跻身于全球任何艺术产区中最常见的“可收藏”民族志艺术对象之列。然而库希勒告诉我们，尽管它们仍以各种形式被制作出来，并且在新爱尔兰当代政治与仪式生活中占据极为重要的地位，但在当地原处几乎见不到任何一件——它们全都在外国人手里，而作为物质对象，它们与原先的制作者已毫无干系。被卖出去换现金是这类对象的最终“死亡”，自十九世纪后几十年起便是如此。从新爱尔兰人的观点看，在概念上，一件完成了其仪式角色的马兰甘雕刻已经腐烂消亡，不复存在；它作为博物馆藏品的未来无关紧要。马兰甘作为社会上显著的对象只“存在”极短的一段时间，即在重要人物的丧葬仪式期间；在此期间，它们通过被雕刻和彩绘而逐渐被注入生命，达于完善，并在丧葬仪式的顶点被展示几个小时——随即又由人们赠出的贝币“杀死”。一旦被“杀死”，它们便不再作为仪式对象存在（这正是它们随后可以被卖给收藏家的原因）。“杀死”马兰甘的那笔贝币，赋予赠送者记住所展示形象的权利；正是这份被内化的形象记忆——在仪式的出资者之间被分割分配——构成了仪式财产（赋予持有者社会特权），在丧葬仪式上被交易，并从长辈一代传递给晚辈一代。
en: There are some 5,000 carvings of the type known as Malangan in collections, which makes them among the commonest ‘collectible' ethnographic art objects from any art-producing region of the globe. Yet Kuchler tells us that, even though they are still produced in various forms, and are to the highest degree salient in contemporary political and ritual life in New Ireland, hardly a single one is actually to be seen in situ there-they are all in the hands of foreigners, and, as physical objects, of no concern to their erstwhile makers. Being sold off for cash is the final ‘death' of objects of this type, and has been since the latter decades of the nineteenth century. Conceptually, from the New Ireland point of view, a Malangan carving which has fulfilled its ritual role has rotted away and is no more, and its future as a museum piece is irrelevant. Malangan only ‘exist' as socially salient objects, for a very short period, during the mortuary ceremonies for important persons, during which they are gradually imbued with life by being carved and painted, brought to perfection and displayed for a few hours at the culminating point of the mortuary ritual-only to be ‘killed' with gifts of shell-money. Once they have been ‘killed' they no longer exist as ritual objects (which is why they may subsequently be sold to collectors). The gift of money which ‘kills' the Malangan entitles the donor to remember the image on display, and it is this internalized memory of the image, parcelled out among the contributors to the ceremony, which constitutes the ceremonial asset-entitling the possessor to social privileges-which is transacted at the mortuary ceremony and transmitted from the senior to the junior generations.

zh: 马兰甘作为一种物质存在只能以天甚至小时来度量的对象，是一种明确具有临时性质的能动性索引。在仪式短暂的持续期间，这件雕刻把构成新爱尔兰北部社会的各占有土地的母系群体成员之间过去与未来关系的密集而持久的网络客观化了。这些土地群体之间的社会关系，建立在成员先前购得的权利之上：记住马兰甘雕刻与母题的权利，从而作为施动者，在后续的马兰甘仪式中（以不同的组合）延续这些母题；在那些仪式上，雕刻又会将这些记忆短暂地化为可见的形象（以多变的组合），并再次以仪式中的给付为条件，在参与者之间交易和分割分配。
en: The Malangan, as an object whose physical existence can thus be measured only in days, or even hours, is an index of agency of an explicitly temporary nature. During the brief duration of the ceremony, the carving objectifies a dense and enduring network of past and future relationships between members of the land-occupying matrilineal units which constitute northern New Ireland society. Social relationships between land-occupying units are legitimized on the basis of members' previously purchased rights to remember Malangan carvings and motifs, and thus to act as agents in perpetuating these motifs (in different combinations) in subsequent Malangan ceremonies, where these memories will again be briefly objectified in carvings (in varied combinations) and again transacted and parcelled out among participants, against ceremonial payments.

zh: 但让我们更仔细地考察马兰甘雕刻。它有若干种类，但我只讨论
中所见的那种常见的彩绘木质类型，其形式是祖先形象辅以各种附属母题。任何一件马兰甘雕刻上出现哪些特定的形式与母题，取决于举办仪式的土地群体的身份，以及这些单位预期未来的特定政治结盟策略——一旦这些联盟通过分割分配马兰甘记忆而获得仪式上的合法化。
en: But let us consider the Malangan carving more closely. There are various kinds, but I shall discuss only the familiar painted wooden variety seen in

, which take the form of ancestral figures accompanied by a variety of subsidiary motifs. Which particular forms and motifs occur on any given Malangan carving depends on the identities of the land-occupying units mounting the ceremony and the particular strategies of political alliance these units anticipate for the future, once these alliances have been ceremonially legitimized by parcelling out Malangan memories.

zh: 马兰甘的目的是为刚去世的重要人物提供一个“身体”，更确切地说，一张“皮”。死亡之际，这样一个人的能动性处于分散状态。用我们的术语说，其能动性的索引大量存在，却没有集中在任何特定之处。死者散布各处的园圃与种植园仍在产出，其财富由各个交换伙伴持有，其房屋仍然矗立，其妻子或丈夫仍与之保持婚姻关系，如此等等。制作雕刻的过程，与地方社会为适应死者退出政治与生产生活的积极参与而进行的重组和调整过程相重合。园圃中的作物被收割，房屋朽坏，继而变成格外丰产的田地，如此等等。也就是说，死者所有分散的“社会效力”——他们曾给周围事物带来的改变——逐渐变成一股可以凝聚在具体物件上的力量。只要有一个物质索引，就能由它溯因推断出这份累积的效力。这就是马兰甘之所是：一种身体，像充了电的电池一样，积聚死者散布于生活世界中的势能。库希勒（1992）把这件雕刻说成死者“生命力”的临时储存库，但我们或许应当指出，“生命”本身与这种生命力并无分别；积聚在马兰甘雕刻中的生命力，是一生社会活动累积下来的结果，而不是一种在范畴上可与日常生活和活动区分开来的神秘能量。
en: The purpose of a Malangan is to provide a ‘body', or more precisely, a ‘skin' for a recently deceased person of importance. On death, the agency of such a person is in a dispersed state. In our terms, indexes of their agency abound, but are not concentrated anywhere in particular. The gardens and plantations of the deceased, scattered here and there, are still in production, their wealth is held by various exchange-partners, their houses are still standing, their wives or husbands are still married to them, and so on. The process of making the carving coincides with the process of reorganization and adjustment through which local society adjusts to the subtraction of the deceased from active participation in political and productive life. The gardens are harvested, the houses decay and become, in turn, particularly productive fields, and so on. That is to say, all the dispersed ‘social effectiveness' of the deceased, the difference they made to how things were, gradually becomes an objectifiable quantity, something to which a single material index may be attached, and from which this accumulated effectiveness may be abducted. This is what the Malangan is; a kind of body which accumulates, like a charged battery, the potential energy of the deceased dispersed in the life-world. Kuchler (1992) speaks of the carving as a temporary repository for the ‘life-force' of the deceased, but we should perhaps observe that there is no difference between ‘life' itself and this life-force; the life-force which accumulates in the Malangan carving is the net result or product of a lifetime's activity in the social world, not a species of mystical energy distinguishable categorically from ordinary life and activity.

zh: 分散的生命靠火聚到马兰甘雕刻这个物质索引中。制作形象的过程被概念化为把火从灰烬逐渐生起，到发红的余烬，再到最终的烈焰（1992: 104）。原木通过加热与灼烧的技术被充入效力（这与用火在成品雕刻上制造极多而复杂的孔洞和空腔的技术用途有关，尤其是在金属工具尚不可得的时代）。随着形式显现（雕刻者是一位受雇的专家，由祖先托来的梦指引），雕刻在概念上变得越来越热。最后一道工序是彩绘，此时雕刻已准备好在最高潮的仪式上重新分配其累积的电荷或“热”；在那个仪式上，它将被公开展示，并被有特权的人记住；也是在那个仪式上，它自身将“死去”，变得冰冷而腐烂。
en: The mechanism for the accumulation of dispersed life into the physical index of the Malangan carving is via the mechanism of fire. The process of making the image is conceptualized as the building up of a fire from ashes, to glowing embers, to the final blaze (1992: 104). The raw wood is charged with efficacy by a technique of heating and burning (this is connected to the technical use of fire to create the very numerous and complicated holes and cavities in the finished carving, especially in the epoch before metal tools were available). As the forms emerge (the carver, a hired specialist, is guided by dreams sent by the ancestors), the carving grows (conceptually) hotter and hotter. The culminating process is painting, at which time the carving is ready to redistribute its accumulated charge or ‘heat' at the climactic ceremony during which it will be publicly displayed and remembered by those privileged to do so, and during which it will, itself, ‘die' and become cold and rotten.

zh: 如我所说，这件雕刻被理解为死者的一张“皮”。皮的概念在这里出于若干原因而至关重要。在新爱尔兰北部，“皮”代表姻亲关系。政治关系（首要的是对土地的控制）建立在由“皮”的纽带所创造的策略性姻亲关系之上——皮代表可交易的人，被分割、重新组合、重新构成的人。（关于“皮”的更多讨论，参见Gell 1993: 23 ff.。）正如库希勒所暗示的，这件雕刻既是容纳祖先生命力的三维实心木质“容器”，同时作为外表面（一个二维场域），又是一张羊皮纸，马兰甘仪式的参与者在其上以红、白、黑三色的特定彩绘装饰的形式，铭刻他们预期的姻亲联盟。正是对雕刻外部彩绘形式的被交易的记忆，将使土地群体之间的未来关系合法化。作为雕刻／容器，马兰甘是过去“社会效力”被积聚和容纳的储存库；作为供人观看的外在形象，马兰甘则投射出这些过去关系将产生的未来——这是马兰甘仪式所促成的某些预期关系（姻亲之间的关系）获得合法化的结果。换言之，马兰甘是能动性由过去传向未来的媒介。尽管雕刻本身只存在于某些（受限的）时空坐标之内，但在概念上，它是一个在时间上分散的对象，一个不在任何特定时间或地点、却穿行于时间与地点之中的对象，就像一场雷暴。
en: The carving, as I mentioned, is understood to be a ‘skin' for the deceased. The concept of a skin is of the utmost importance here, for a number of reasons. In northern New Ireland, ‘skin' stands for affinal relations. Political relationships (primarily, control over land) are founded on strategic affinal relationships created by ties of ‘skin’—skin stands for the transactable person, the person divided up, recombined, and reconstituted. (For more on ‘skin' cf. Gell 1993: 23 ff.) The carving, as Kuchler implies, is both a three-dimensional, solid wooden ‘container' for ancestral life-force, but at the same time, as an external surface (a two-dimensional field) it is a parchment on which participants in the Malangan ceremony inscribe their anticipated affinal alliances, in the form of specific painted decorations in red, white, and black. It is the transacted memory of the external, painted form of the carving which will legitimize future relationships between land-occupying units. As a carving/container, the Malangan is a repository of past ‘social effectiveness' accumulated and contained, while as a spectacle, an exterior, the Malangan projects the future that these past relationships will produce, as a result of the legitimization of certain anticipated relationships (between affines) that the Malangan ceremony enables. The Malangan, in other words, mediates and transmits agency between past and future. Though the carving itself exists only within certain (restricted) time-space coordinates, conceptually, it is a temporally dispersed object, an object at no specific time or place, but moving through time and place, like a thunderstorm.

zh: 但“皮”的观念还有一层附加的意义，读者或许已经注意到了。让我们来到最高潮的时刻：仪式参与者目睹雕刻的最终形式，并把它记在心里。在这一刻，有特权的人（支付了相应仪式款项的人）获得“马兰甘的知识”——即不仅复制马兰甘可见形式的权利，还有复制这一可见形式所索引的社会关系（包括土地权利）的权利。用来指称这种取得这些权利的知识的词是wune，它的含义之一是“烟”。由于雕刻在这一阶段的表面已被火与热充塞到几乎爆裂，那么用来描述效力从雕刻（索引）传递给接受者（观看者）的用火来作比，也就毫不令人费解了。但我们也不由自主地想起前文（7.4节）引用的卢克莱修的话：他把物的“飞散拟像”——从物中发出、使我们得以知觉物的“偶像”——与“［小物体］处于松散扩散状态，像橡木柴、热与火发出的烟”联系起来。伊壁鸠鲁派模型意味着，物的形象是物的可扩散部分，正如烟是燃烧木柴的可扩散部分。卢克莱修把热与烟的发出——从对象而来的无形式的、近乎物质的弥散——与更熟悉的具有可见形式的“偶像”联系起来，这种联系在新爱尔兰思想中几乎魔术般地重演了。因为wune（作为强有力的知识）不仅是从雕刻火热表面散发出的“烟”；它同样也是可见形式的“相似性”（拟像），是被内化为记忆形象的雕刻之“皮”。
en: But the notion of ‘skin' has an additional significance, which may not have escaped the reader. Let us proceed to the climactic moment, at which the participants in the ceremony witness the carving in its final form and register its memory. At this moment, the privileged ones (the ones who have made the appropriate ritual payments) receive ‘the knowledge of Malangan'-that is, the right to reproduce not just the visible form of Malangan but the social relations, including land-rights, which this visible form indexes. The word which is used to refer to this empowering knowledge is wune, which, among other things, means ‘smoke'. Since the carving has, at this stage, a surface charged to bursting with fire and heat, it is in no way puzzling to find that the idiom used to describe the transmission of potency from the carving (index) to the recipient (spectator) is a fiery one. But we also find, irresistibly recalled to mind, the words of Lucretius cited earlier (Sect. 7.4) in which he associates the ‘flying simulacra' of things, the ‘idols' which are emitted from things and which enable us to perceive them, with ‘[little bodies] in a state of loose diffusion, like smoke which logs of oak, heat and fires emit'. The Epicurean model implies that images of things are diffusible parts of things, just as smoke is a diffusible part of burning logs. Lucretius' association between the emission of heat and smoke—formless, quasi-material diffusion from the object--and the more familiar ‘idols' which have visible form is recapitulated, almost magically, in New Ireland thought. For wune (as powerful knowledge) is not just the ‘smoke' which emanates from the fiery surface of the carving; equally it is ‘likeness' (the simulacra) in visible form, the ‘skin' of the carving which is internalized as a memory image.

zh: 马兰甘雕刻是一个以皮为身的偶像，它像“蝉薄纱般的蜕壳”一样，以准物质的形式分布于观看者的记忆之中；观看者把祖先的“皮”内化为自己的新“皮”，一张预期着与姻亲伙伴建立新“皮”关系的新皮。记住形象是在内部长出一张新皮的方式，从而把一个新的身份投射到未来。可怜的培尔·金特（上文7.11节）只能经由易卜生剧中讲述的种种纷繁变故来获得他的新皮，结果是记忆的皮在他一生中逐层积累，而他连同他的洋葱一起把这些皮拆解了。新爱尔兰人的做法不同，因为他们已有意识地把交换“记忆”发展为公开的策略；记忆的累积是制度化的，而不像培尔·金特那样是偶然的产物。他们累积的、相互咬合的记忆由内在的皮构成，经由马兰甘中介，可以随意拆开并重新配置。
en: The Malangan carving is a skin-idol, which like the ‘gossamer coats of cicadas' is distributed in quasi-material form in the memories of the onlookers, who internalize the ancestral ‘skin' as a new ‘skin' of their own, a new skin which anticipates new ‘skin' relationships with affinal partners. Memorizing the image is a way of growing a new skin internally and thus projecting a new identity into the future. Poor Peer Gynt (above, Sect. 7.11) could only acquire his new skins by undergoing all the manifold vicissitudes related in Ibsen's play, resulting in the biographical accumulation of memory-skins which he disassembles along with his onion. New Irelanders proceed differently, for they have elaborated the art of transacting ‘memories' as a conscious, public, strategy; the accumulation of memories is institutionalized rather than being the product of happenstance, like Peer Gynt's. Their accumulated, interlocking memories consist of internal skins, mediated via the Malangan, which can be taken apart and reconfigured at will.

zh: 这发生在传递的最高潮时刻：被火激活的马兰甘表面，以卢克莱修式拟像的形式消散，这些拟像或多或少作为内在身体部件，被有特权的观看者内化；观看者由此接受的实体——不仅是祖先身体的实体，还有死者全部的施动能力——供未来重新部署。这可以说是从索引中对能动性的最高溯因，因为他者的能动性不仅是经由索引被承受；它还由此被延续和再生产。于是记忆成为一种通过社会制度塑造出来的媒介，传递改变世界、塑造事件进程的力量，而不再只是对过去的被动登记。一旦索引在其“充电”状态被目睹过，它便像耗尽了力量的尸体，因为无论其他人对它形成什么样的记忆形象（通过在博物馆或商店里目睹它的惰性状态），那些都不会是那些记忆——那些被唯一地规定为有力量、有效力的记忆。
en: This happens at the climactic moment of transmission, as the surface of the Malangan, animated by fire, is dissipated in the form of Lucretian simulacra which are internalized, more or less as internal body parts, by the privileged onlookers, who, in this way, receive the substance-not just of the ancestral body, but the entire agentive capacity of the deceased-for future redeployment. This is, as it were, the supreme abduction of agency from the index, in that the other's agency is not just suffered via the index; it is also thereby perpetuated and reproduced. Thus memory becomes a socially engineered medium for the transmission of the power to change the world and shape the course of events, rather than a mere passive registration of the past. Once the index has been witnessed in its ‘charged' state, it is a mere corpse, drained of its power, because whatever memory images others may form of it (by witnessing it in its inert condition in a museum or a shop) they will not be those memories, the ones uniquely stipulated as potent and efficacious.

zh: 马兰甘艺术的例子是有用的，因为它能开始动摇我们在物质文化方面通常所作的物质与心智（或认知）之间的区分。马兰甘无可争辩地是物质对象，但在当地社会发挥作用的马兰甘，是新爱尔兰人装在头脑里随身携带的内化形象。作为物质对象存在，只是马兰甘生命史中的一个过渡阶段；它的大部分存在是作为记忆痕迹，或者用更地道的说法，作为一张内在的“皮”。新爱尔兰北部本土的马兰甘——而不是收藏中的马兰甘——正在四处走动，开辟园圃、发表政治演说、与人交换财物、结婚生子；然而悖谬的是，它们完全无法为外部民族志观察所及。只有对过去、现在与预期中的马兰甘仪式及相关的亲属关系与土地交易进行一项大规模调查——库希勒在我写作之际正在完成这项工作——才能揭示马兰甘的理想形式：一个社会性分布的记忆形象的区域系统。
en: The example of Malangan art is useful in that it can start to undermine the distinction we commonly make between the material and the mental (or cognitive) with respect to material culture. The Malangan are indisputably material objects, but the socially relevant Malangan are internalized images which New Irelanders carry about inside their heads. Being a material object is merely a transitional phase in the biography of a Malangan, most of whose existence is as a memory trace, or, more idiomatically, as an internal ‘skin'. The Malangans of northern New Ireland itself-rather than the Malangans in collections-are walking about, making gardens and political speeches, engaging in exchange transactions, marrying and having children, yet, paradoxically, they are not accessible to external ethnographic observation at all. Only an extended survey of past, present, and prospective Malangan ceremonies, and the associated kinship and land transactions-which Kuchler is completing as I write-will reveal the ideal form of Malangan as a regional system of socially distributed memory images.

zh: 我们眼下暂且不沿这条线索往下追问，但我们可以把注意力转向类似的艺术品区域分布系统（这一次由持久的对象而非记忆形象构成），它们构成一个动态整体，由此继续这一总主题——借助南希·芒恩（1977, 1986）的若干著名研究。
en: We, meanwhile, cannot pursue this fascinating prospect, but we can continue the general theme by turning our attention to similar systems of regionally distributed artworks (this time, consisting of enduring objects, rather than memory images) forming a dynamic whole, by referring to certain well-known studies by Nancy Munn (1977, 1986).

zh: 9.3　加瓦的库拉
en: 9.3　Gawan Kula

zh: 南希·芒恩的研究在本讨论的语境中尤为突出，因为她在一系列研究中特别关注物质索引——加瓦独木舟与库拉贵重物——与（社会）时空之间的关系。我即将展开的论证正是围绕这一问题。我的论点是：“认知”，或更确切地说意识，是一种心智过程，主观时间性经由意识经验随时间转化的过程而得以构成。在下一节我将简要介绍胡塞尔的心智模型，即心智作为知觉与记忆中的形象发生一连串“变样”。与此同时，我主张，存在并流通于外部社会世界中的“能动性索引”，可以说创造了一个索引间的时空场，它承载着类似的结构，也就是说，它同样由内容（形象）随时间的一系列转化构成。这一论点稍后将以马塞尔·杜尚的作品与毛利会堂来具体说明。但在我们能够展开这一论证之前，进一步考察艺术品（或其他能动性索引）与时空之关系的问题会有所助益。在这一领域芒恩作出了若干非常重要的贡献。
en: Nancy Munn's work is particularly salient in the context of this discussion, in that she has devoted particular attention in a series of studies, to the relationship between material indexes-Gawan canoes and Kula valuables-and (social) space-time. The argument on which I am embarking turns on this issue. My thesis is that ‘cognition', or more precisely, consciousness, is a mental process through which subjective temporality is constituted via a process of transformation of conscious experience over time. In the next section I shall briefly present Husserl's model of the mind as a series of ‘modifications' of perceptual memory images. Concurrently, I am arguing that the ‘indexes of agency' which exist and circulate in the external social world create, so to speak, an inter-indexical space-time field which bears an analogous structure, that is to say that it, too, consists of a series of transformations of contents (images) over time. This thesis will be instantiated later, with regard to the works of Marcel Duchamp and Maori meeting houses. But before we are in a position to embark on this argument, it would be helpful to consider further the question of the relation between artworks (or other indexes of agency) and space-time. In this area Munn has made certain very important contributions.

zh: 南希·芒恩的论文《加瓦独木舟的时空转化》（1977）追溯了加瓦独木舟的生命史：它们起初是生长在某一氏族所持土地上的树木，由其他氏族的成员制成独木舟（在此过程中经由加瓦内部的交换路径流动）。一旦制成独木舟，它们便进入加瓦内部更进一步的交换路径。在这里它们被用来交换薯蓣，这些薯蓣从嫁出女子的母系世系群送到迎娶女子的母系世系群。因此在某种意义上，独木舟在加瓦被转化为薯蓣，而在加瓦之外它们被转化为贝壳贵重物——这些贵重物由其最终使用者（所谓“库拉环”中其他岛屿的男子，他们用独木舟进行海外（岛际）交换）拿来交换独木舟。
en: Nancy Munn's article ‘The Spatiotemporal Transformation of Gawa Canoes' (1977) traces the biography of Gawa canoes, which start life as trees growing on the land held by a particular clan and are fashioned into canoes by members of other clans (moving through exchange pathways internal to Gawa in the process). Once made into canoes, they enter further exchange pathways within Gawa. Here they are transacted against the yams which are transmitted from wife-giving matrilines to wife-receiving ones. So in a sense, the canoes are converted into yams on Gawa, while outside Gawa they are converted into shell valuables- which are exchanged for them by their eventual users, men from other islands in the so-called ‘Kula Ring' who use them for carrying on overseas (inter-island) exchanges.

zh: 从已经把一艘航海独木舟交换成若干贝壳贵重物（这些贵重物本身将在海外交换中流通）的加瓦母系世系群的观点看，这艘独木舟仍然被“拥有”；但它是以另一种形式被拥有，即作为贝壳贵重物而非作为木舟。芒恩在这里察觉到一个持续的去物质化过程。此前还是一棵沉重、扎根于土中的大树的独木舟，逐渐变成完全非物质的东西，或更确切地说，物质但不受拘限的东西。也就是说，独木舟被转化为一个“影响场”。这个场由独木舟所转化成的库拉交换贵重物所施加的磁力生成。由于这些贵重物是该氏族所有、不受他人权利约束的财产（一类被称为kitoum的财产），它们有能力把其他（不同来源与类型的）贵重物朝加瓦的方向移动，并且互惠地，当它们向外旅行时，把加瓦的名字与声誉传扬到远方。芒恩主张，它们最终被转化为她所称的“社会时间性的时空”。这种时空与其说是由若干维度构成的空间，不如说是一个力场（如电磁场），由价值对象（能动性索引）施加，这些对象最终附着于有权势的人，却在环境中流通。这个场构成了交易空间，被持续运动、经历相继变形的对象所产生的多重力量所极化。每一件kitoum（不受他人权利约束的贵重物）都可追溯到拥有母系世系群的一个成员，他构成其社会附着点，在那里它不再是一个被解放的对象，而成为一个人的可分割组成部分，即可说是回到从那个人身上分出前的位置。
en: From the point of view of the Gawa matriline which has exchanged a seagoing canoe for certain shell valuables (valuables that will themselves be circulated in overseas exchanges) the canoe is still ‘owned'; but it is owned in another form, as shell valuables rather than as a wooden canoe. Munn detects a consistent process of de-materialization here. The canoe that was, heretofore, a heavy, rooted, earthy thing, a massive tree, becomes, by degrees, something totally immaterial, or rather, material but unconfined. That is, the canoe is converted into a ‘field of influence'. This field is generated by the magnetism exerted by the Kula-exchange valuables into which the canoe has been converted. By virtue of being the unencumbered property of the owning clan (a type of property designated as kitoum) these valuables have the power to move other valuables (of different origin and type) in the direction of Gawa, and reciprocally, as they travel outwards, carrying the name and fame of Gawa far and wide. Munn argues that they are converted ultimately into what she calls ‘sociotemporal space-time'. This space-time is not so much a dimensional manifold as a field of forces (like an electromagnetic field) exerted by objects of value (indexes of agency) ultimately attached to powerful persons but circulating in the milieu. This field constitutes transactional space polarized by the multiple forces generated by objects in continuous motion and undergoing successive metamorphoses. Each of these kitoum (unencumbered valuables) is traceable to a member of the owning matriline, who constitutes its social point of attachment, where it ceases to be a liberated object and becomes a partible component of a person, its original hole, so to speak.

zh: 库拉参与者，即参与库拉贵重物（臂镯与项链）岛际与内部交换的人，是一个在时空上延展的人。自马林诺夫斯基最初的描述（1922）以来，库拉体系的实际运作机制已被讨论得如此之多，以至于这里几乎无需提供详细说明。只需说，参与该体系的男子之所以参与，是因为他们能主张对kitoum的所有权，即作为他们自己不受他人权利约束的仪式财产的库拉贵重物，而不是他们作为两个kitoum持有者之间的中介可能持有的贵重物。kitoum所有者与所持贵重物之间的关系是不可分离的，仿佛kitoum是一个身体部件，但与此同时kitoum又是一个可以作为交换物品传往海外、可以在时空中自由流通、可以转化为另一对象的对象。然而与原所有者的附着持续存在，因为重要的kitoum是被个别命名、被识别的对象，无论kitoum从一岛旅行到另一岛，其所有者的名字也将随之旅行。kitoum持有者把他的kitoum插入他所能进入的某条交换“路径”（keda），以换取回礼，这些回礼并不与kitoum本身匹配，而是一种租金，由接受者支付，以换取充当把这件有声望的kitoum转送至其最终目的地的中介的特权。于是产生了一股与kitoum通行方向相反的财富流。但最终，在经过不同库拉社区许多人之手后，kitoum将遇到体系中另一件与之匹配、声望相等的贵重物。这将是另一件kitoum，是某个遥远岛屿上一位同样重要的人的不受他人权利约束的财产。当这种情况发生时，原初的kitoum（比方说一件臂镯）将与另一件与它相配的 kitoum “成婚”（那将是一条项链，因为臂镯只能交换项链，反之亦然），而项链将开始朝原初kitoum持有者的方向回返，沿途再次经过许多中介，并建立起进一步的反向财富流。库拉参与者的目标是获得对众多kitoum的控制，操纵交换路径，以设法使他们的“名字”——附着于有声望的贵重物——传扬远方。如果一个人因掌握著名贵重物的流通路径而在远方享有声望，他就能够影响远方库拉参与者的算计。可以说，他不止是一个仅仅具身的人。他是一个在各处延展的人，在此处、彼处、无处不在，因为他的名字附着于流通的对象，更因为这些对象的运动在长距离上受他的意向能动性、他的算计、以及（魔力辅助的）说服的影响（Munn 1986）。
en: A Kula operator, one who participates in the inter-island and internal exchanges in Kula valuables (arm-shells and necklaces) is a spatio-temporally extended person. The actual mechanics of the Kula system have been discussed so often since Malinowski's original description (1922) that it is hardly necessary to provide a detailed account here. Suffice it to say that men who participate in the system do so because they can lay claim to ownership of kitoum, that is, Kula valuables which are their own unencumbered ritual property, not valuables which they may be holding as intermediaries between one kitoum-holder and another. The relationship between kitoum-owner and the valuable which is held is indissociable, as if the kitoum were a body-part, but at the same time the kitoum is an object that can be transmitted abroad as an exchange item, that can circulate freely in space and time, and that can be converted into another object. The attachment to the original owner persists, however, because important kitoum are individually named, recognized, objects, and wherever the kitoum travels from island to island, the name of its owner will travel with it as well. The kitoum-holder inserts his kitoum into one of the exchange ‘pathways' (keda) to which he has access, in exchange for return gifts which do not match the kitoum itself, but which are a sort of rent, paid by the recipient, for the privilege of being the one to serve as intermediary in the forwarding of this prestigious kitoum to its ultimate destination. Thus a flow of wealth is generated in the opposite direction to the passage of the kitoum. Eventually, though, after passing through many hands, in different Kula communities, the kitoum will encounter another valuable in the system which matches it, being equal in renown. This will be another kitoum, the unencumbered property of an equally important man on some distant island. When this happens, the original kitoum (an arm-shell, let us say) will ‘marry' its opposite-number kitoum (which would be a necklace, because an arm-shell can only be exchanged for a necklace and vice versa) and the necklace, will begin to travel back towards the original kitoum-holder, again passing through many intermediaries along the way and setting up further countervailing flows of wealth. The aim of Kula operators is to gain control of numerous kitoum, manipulating the pathways of exchange so as to contrive that their ‘names'-attached to prestigious valuables-travel far and wide. A man whose name is known in distant communities as one who controls the pathways along which renowned valuables are transferred, can influence the calculations of Kula operators in faraway places. He is, so to speak, more than a merely incarnate man. He is an expanded and disseminated being, present here, there, and everywhere because his name is attached to circulating objects, and still more because the movements of these objects are influenced, at long range, by his intentional agency, his calculativeness, and (magically assisted) persuasion (Munn 1986).

zh: 与库拉参与者名字相联系的库拉贵重物，被概念化为他作为具有支配力量的人的身体在场的索引；从它们，远方的接受者不仅溯因出他的力量，还有他的身体之美，因为这些库拉贵重物毕竟是身体装饰也是身体部件，它们被视为美丽，也视为古老而有声望。作为一个分布于各处的人，库拉参与者吸引财富如同年轻男子吸引情人；他人的心智被这种从远方传来的魅力所左右，而这种爱的信物，以贵重物的形式，疾速奔向他。芒恩（1983）告诉我们，库拉贵重物的等级体系对应于库拉参与者的等级体系。应用于贵重物的等级图式，把较新、无声望、几乎没有经年打磨与把玩而来的金色包浆、尚未与许多名人名字相联系的物品，与古老、被珍视的物品对立起来，后者有力地唤起那些通过库拉超越了时空、永恒地有力、有魅力、有影响力的人的身份。一件重要的臂镯或项链并非以象征的方式“代表”某个重要人物；实际上它就是一个重要人物，因为年岁、影响力、以及某种类似“智慧”的东西内在于它的物质实体、它光滑而有包浆的表面，正如它们内在于它所附着、并作为分布式人格的偶像从之飞走的那位名人的心智与身体。（再一次，我们可以把作为迁徙性身体索引的库拉贵重物与卢克莱修的飞散拟像作类比。）
en: The Kula valuables which are associated with a Kula operator's name are conceptualized as indexes of his bodily presence as a person of commanding powers; from them, distant recipients abduct not just his power but his bodily beauty, for these Kula valuables are, after all, body-decorations as well as body-parts, and they are regarded as beautiful as well as ancient and prestigious. As a distributed person, the Kula operator attracts wealth as a young man attracts lovers; others’ minds are swayed by his long-range allure and tokens of this love, in the form of valuables, speed towards him. Munn (1983) tells us that the ranking system of Kula valuables corresponds to the ranking system of Kula operators. The ranking scheme applied to valuables opposes new-ish, non-prestigious, items with little of the golden patina that comes from years of polishing and handling, and which have yet to be associated with the names of many famous men, to ancient, treasured items, which powerfully evoke the identities of men who, through Kula, have transcended time and space, who are timelessly potent, attractive, and influential. An important arm-shell or necklace does not ‘stand for' someone important, in a symbolic way; to all intents and purposes it is an important person in that age, influence, and something like ‘wisdom' inheres in its physical substance, in its smooth and patinated surfaces, just as they do in the mind and body of the man of renown to whom it was attached, and from whom it has flown away as an idol of distributed personhood. (Once again, we can draw an analogy between the Kula valuable as a migratory bodily index and the flying simulacra of Lucretius.)

zh: 但我们不能把只谈人格怎样分布，忽略支撑这一切的能动性。一个人如何在实践中成为杰出的库拉参与者，一个能在远距离“打动人心”、支配一片广阔的社会时空的人？一个人如何变得如此迷人地有吸引力、如此不可抗拒地有说服力，以至于岛际交换的路径不可阻挡地朝期望的方向汇聚？唯有通过知识、智力与算计。要想成功，库拉参与者必须具备从事策略行动的卓越能力，这需要一个关于库拉贵重物在其中移动的外部场的全面内部模型（参见Gell 1992a: 280-5）。操作者必须能够理解多样而极其复杂的交换场，必须能够记住无数过去的交换历史并评估其结果。他必须构建精确预期未来、指导策略干预的“假如”情景。换言之，他的心智必须作为一个模拟装置运作——而这确实是一切心智或多或少都在做的——呈现过去、现在与未来的库拉交易总体的概观。
en: But we cannot place the whole weight of the discussion on the ‘distributedness' of distributed personhood, at the expense of the core of agency which lies at its heart. How does one, in practice, become a great Kula operator, a man able to ‘move minds' at great distances and dominate an expanded region of social space and time? How does one become so enchantingly attractive, so irresistibly persuasive, that the paths of inter-island exchange converge ineluctably in the desired direction? Only through knowledge, intelligence, and calculation. For success to accrue, the Kula operator must possess a superior capacity to engage in strategic action, which necessitates a comprehensive internal model of the external field within which Kula valuables move about (cf. Gell 1992a: 280-5). The operator must be able to comprehend the manifold and inordinately complex field of exchanges, must be able to remember innumerable past histories of exchanges, and evaluate their outcomes. He must construct ‘what if' scenarios that anticipate the future with precision, guiding strategic intervention. His mind, in other words, must work as a simulation device -and this indeed is what all minds do, more or less-presenting a synoptic view of the totality of Kula transactions, past, present, and to come.

zh: 参与者必须在心中重建一套可实际运用的拟像——一幅库拉交易迷宫的动态时空地图，以便以梦游般的灵巧，知道该拉动哪些微妙的线。一切都取决于内在策略意图（植根于累积的经验与记忆）与历史地生产出来的“外部”世界——心智在交换对象中被客观化、在其中扩展、相遇、竞争的真实世界——之间的连贯性。成功的库拉参与者控制库拉世界，因为他的心智已变得与那个世界同延。他已把它的因果网内化为自己作为一个人、作为一个独立施动者的存在的一部分。“内部”（心智过程）与“外部”（以具体物件体现的人格的交换）已融合在一起；心智与实在合一，而且——说得直白些——某种类似神性的东西是可以达到的。这种通过扩展的、客观化的能动性与真实世界错综复杂的因果网融合而实现的（相对）神化，在我看来是库拉的终极目标。它至少向我提示了通往超越的路径，这些路径对我们这些世俗的灵魂与顽固的唯物主义者，与对参与库拉交易的美拉尼西亚岛屿居民一样可达，但那只是题外话。我想从这一切中提取的论点更为有限。它仅仅是：当我们考察库拉体系所建立于其上的扩展的、可交易的“人”与人格时，我们被迫认识到“心智”既有主观的存在方式，表现为思绪、意图和心智状态等转瞬即逝的相继出现，也有客观的存在方式，体现于可以交换的物件所构成的格局。在这里，这些物件就是人格的索引，如臂镯和项链。库拉体系整体是一种认知形式，它发生在身体之外，扩散于时空之中，并经由物质索引及涉及它们的交易的媒介而进行。
en: In his own person, the operator must reconstruct a working simulacrum-a dynamic space-time map of the maze of Kula transactions, so that, with somnambulistic dexterity, he knows which delicate strings to pull. Everything depends on the coherence of inner strategic intentions grounded in accumulated experience and memory, and the historically produced world ‘out there'-the real world in which minds, objectified in exchange objects, expand, meet, and contend. The successful Kula operator controls the world of Kula because his mind has become coextensive with that world. He has internalized its causal texture as part of his being as a person and as an independent agent. ‘Internal' (mental processes) and ‘outside' (transactions in objectified personhood) have fused together; mind and reality are one, and-not to put too fine a point on it-something like godhead is achievable. This (relative) divinization through the fusing together of an expanded, objectified agency, and the myriad causal texture of the real world seems to me to be the ultimate objective of Kula. It suggests, to me at any rate, pathways towards transcendence which are as accessible to us, secular souls and die-hard materialists, as to the inhabitants of the Melanesian islands which participate in Kula transactions, but that is only by the by. The point that I wish to extract from all this is more limited. It is simply that when we come to consider the expanded, transactable, ‘persons' and personhood on which the Kula system is founded, we are brought to recognize that ‘mind' can exist objectively as well as subjectively; that is, as a pattern of transactable objects-indexes of personhood, in this instance, arm-shells, and necklaces-as well as a fleeting succession of ‘thoughts', 'intentions', ‘mental states', etc. The Kula system as a whole is a form of cognition, which takes place outside the body, which is diffused in space and time, and which is carried on through the medium of physical indexes and transactions involving them.

zh: 9.4　作为分布式对象的艺术家作品全集
en: 9.4　The Artist’s Œuvre as a Distributed Object

zh: 让我们从对大洋洲“分布式对象”与“分布式人格”实例的考察，转向一个更贴近我们自身的例子。我们西方人最熟悉的一种“分布式对象”（索引一个分布式人格）——著名艺术家全部作品构成的“全集”。任何有声望的艺术家都由众多作品代表，这些作品散见于各种收藏，也能够为回顾展而重新汇集，或以附完整作品总目的豪华版出版。
en: Let us turn from the consideration of Oceanic instances of ‘distributed objects' and ‘distributed personhood' to an example closer to home. We, in the West, are familiar with one form of ‘distributed object' (indexing a distributed person) above all-the œuvre or ‘complete works' of famous artists. Any artist of renown is represented by numerous works, disseminated in various collections, and also capable of being reassembled for retrospective exhibitions, or published in a de luxe edition with a complete catalogue raisonné.

zh: 让我们考察一位艺术家作品全集的典型构成——我们最熟悉的那类艺术家，即具有鲜明个人风格与专门关注其作品的批评者的后文艺复兴职业艺术家。艺术家的全集主要由一系列完成作品构成，它们可能产于不同地点，随后分布于众多收藏。这些完成作品通常有纪年或可断代，可被归入一个年代序列：早期作品、中期作品、晚期作品，等等。因此艺术家的全集既在空间上分散，也在时间上分散。艺术家死后，一旦全集完成，它便仿佛构成一个一段独立的时空，可以经由每件作品个别地进入，每件作品都以索引的方式代表全部作品及其生产的历史与个人生命史语境。
en: Let us consider the characteristic make-up of an artist's oeuvre, an artist of the kind with which we are most familiar, a post-Renaissance professional artist with a distinctive personal style and a personal critical following. The artist’s œuvre consists primarily of a series of finished works, produced, it may be, at different places, and subsequently distributed in numerous collections. These finished works are usually dated or datable, and can be assigned to a chronological sequence, early works, middle-period works, late works, and so on. So the artist's oeuvre is both spatially dispersed and temporally dispersed. After the artist's death, once the œuvre is complete, it constitutes, as it were, an independent chunk of space-time, which can be accessed via each work individually, each standing, indexically, for all of them and the historical-biographical context of their production.

zh: 但艺术家的全集并不只由各自作为独立实体的完成作品构成。如果我们研究许多著名艺术家的作品（如列奥纳多、米开朗基罗、康斯太布尔），会发现就数量而言，大部分是为完成作品所作的“准备性习作”，而非完成作品本身。而且，这些表面上“临时”的技术习作——不是为艺术公众而是为画室私用而作——所被赋予的历史价值，与完成作品所被赋予的价值一样大，甚至更大（拍卖行价格另当别论）。从历史的观点看，这些准备性草图是无价的，因为它们让我们了解艺术家构思并完成公开展出作品的认知过程。此外，它们往往是艺术家风格底层发展趋势、乃至艺术中更广泛历史趋势发展的关键指针（如康斯太布尔的草图与后来十九世纪艺术——包括印象派等——之间的关系）。有了草图和作品的暂定版本，我们便能看到创作怎样在艺术家的认知时间和生命史中逐步展开。
en: But the artist’s œuvre does not consist exclusively of finished works each one of which stands as an independent entity. If we study the output of many famous artists (e.g. Leonardo, Michelangelo, Constable) we find that numerically speaking the greater part consists of ‘preparatory studies' for finished works, rather than finished works themselves. Moreover, the historical value placed on these ostensibly ‘provisional' technical studies, not produced for the art public but for private use in the studio, is as great, or even greater, than the value placed on the finished works (saleroom prices are another matter). From an historical point of view, these preparatory sketches are invaluable, because they inform us about the cognitive processes of generation of the finished works produced for public exhibition. Moreover, they are often crucial pointers to the underlying trend of development of the artist's style, and indeed the development of wider historical trends in art (e.g. the relationship between Constable's sketches and later nineteenth-century art, including Impressionism, etc.). The availability of sketches and provisional versions of works allows us insight into artistic activity as a process unfolding over (cognitive and biographical) time.

zh: 同时，我刚才在“准备性习作”与“完成作品”之间所作的区分并非绝对。因为我们知道完成作品的日期，我们也能够把这些完成作品同时看作后来作品的“准备性习作”。因此，塞尚早期的“浴者”以及他的某些风景画，虽然是独立构思的，实际上却充当了《大浴女》的准备性习作——在这件作品中塞尚试图概括并进一步发展此前二三十年里陆续所作的尝试。
en: Meanwhile, the distinction I have just drawn between ‘preparatory studies' and ‘finished works' is not absolute. Because we know the dates of finished works, we are also able to see these finished works as being, simultaneously, ‘preparatory studies' for later works. Thus, Cezanne's earlier ‘bathers', and certain of his landscapes, while conceived independently, actually serve as preparatory studies for Les Grandes Baigneuses—a work in which Cezanne tries to epitomize, and further develop, a long series of previous experiments over twenty or thirty years.

zh: 许多艺术家以可识别的系列创作，在其职业生涯中有意识地演进对某一特定母题的独特处理。例如布拉克从1930年代起开始画以“艺术家画室”为主题（以画架上的画布为特征）的画；这一系列在20世纪50至60年代达到顶点，产生若干综合布拉克成熟风格的难忘杰作。我们也有毕加索、培根、莫奈、马蒂斯等的著名“系列”。换言之，艺术作品经常构成时间系列的“环节”，不仅因为它们是可断代的对象（起源于特定时空坐标），而且因为它们形成世系；它们是全集中其他作品的祖先与后裔。合在一起，它们构成一个宏观对象或时间对象，随时间演进。
en: Many artists produce works in recognizable series, consciously evolving a distinctive treatment of a particular motif over the course of their career. Braque, for instance, started painting pictures on the theme ‘the artist's studio' (featuring a canvas on an easel) from the 1930s onwards; this series culminates in the 1950s and 1960s in a number of unforgettable masterpieces which synthesize Braque's mature style. We also have famous ‘series' from Picasso, Bacon, Monet, Matisse, etc. In other words, it is frequently the case that works of art form ‘moments' of temporal series, not just because they are datable objects (originating at certain space-time coordinates) but because they form lineages; they are ancestral to, and descended from, other works in the œuvre. Taken together, they form a macro-object, or temporal object, which evolves over time.

zh: 最后，我们可以注意到，艺术家全集的构成成分不仅在时间中“向前”指，如“准备性草图”预示完成作品，或培根的第一幅“教皇”指向他后来的“教皇”。艺术家在制作新作品时也“记得”先前作品，“引用”自己，甚至生产先前作品的彻底复制品与摹本。我们不知道列奥纳多《岩间圣母》两个版本（伦敦的那件或巴黎的那件）哪件是原作哪件是摹本；所能确定的只是两者展示同等程度的技术卓越，且两者同样都是“列奥纳多”。艺术家如今因“重复自己”而受批评家斥责，因为这被认为亏待了要求持续创新的公众。但实际上所有艺术实践都不可避免地依赖反复沿用过去的东西，否则“风格”概念（它依赖全集中所有作品之间某种程度的相似）将无法应用。没有重复，艺术将失去记忆。的确，“准备性习作”概念本身就意味着艺术家随后将“复制”自己先前的作品（以私下“习作”格式），以便生产随后的“公开”作品。因此艺术家全集中作品之间时间联系的网指向两个方向。任何一件艺术作品，粗略地说，在其制作者全集的语境中考察，都既可能是后来作品的“准备”，又是先前作品的“重演”。
en: Finally, we may notice that the constituents of an artist’s œuvre do not just point ‘forwards' in time, as the ‘preparatory sketch' points upstream towards the finished work, or Bacon's first ‘Pope' points towards his later ‘Popes'. Artists also ‘remember' previous works in making new ones, ‘quote' themselves, and even produce downright copies and replicas of previous work. We do not know which of the two versions of The Virgin of the Rocks by Leonardo (the one in London or the one in Paris) is the original and which is the copy; all that can be said for sure is that both display the same degree of technical excellence, and both equally are ‘Leonardos'. Artists are nowadays reprimanded by critics for ‘repeating themselves' since this is considered short-changing the public who demand continuous innovation. But actually all artistic practice is inevitably dependent on wholesale repetition, otherwise the concept of ‘style' (which depends on some degree of resemblance between all the works in an œuvre) would be impossible to apply. Without repetition, art would lose its memory. Indeed, the concept of a ‘preparatory study' implies, in itself, that the artist will subsequently ‘copy' his own previous work (in private, ‘study' format) so as to produce the subsequent ‘public' work. So the mesh of temporal connections between the works in an artist’s œuvre points in both directions. Any given work of art, in gross terms, considered in the context of its maker’s œuvre, is likely to be both a ‘preparation' for later works, and a ‘recapitulation' of previous works.

zh: 然而，既要讨论创作怎样预示后来作品，也要讨论它怎样回顾以前的作品时，我们能够使这一思想更精确一点。需要作一个区分：一方面是在设计一件以具体方式设想的后续作品过程中产生的“准备性习作”，另一方面是“先驱”作品和后来的作品之间较弱的联系——“先驱”原本是独立创作的，后来才显出与某件作品一脉相承。创作它时，艺术家并未具体设想后来的作品。虽然在实践中“准备性草图”与后续作品“先驱”之间可能有渐变，但它们仍可作为理想类型对立。同样，我们可以把“艺术家摹本”（如《岩间圣母》的较晚版本）——带着明确复制先前作品的想法而生产——与先前作品的无意复制对立起来，后者是新作品起源的必要特征；也就是说，画家意图生产新作品，却复制了自己先前的作品，因为风格连贯性与绘画实践（根深蒂固的艺术习惯）要求如此。再一次，在现实中有意复制与无意重演之间有渐变，但理想类型的区分可以保留。
en: However, where both artistic projection and artistic retrospection are at issue, we are able to render this thought a little more precise. There is a distinction to be drawn between, say, a ‘preparatory study' which is produced in the process of designing a subsequent work which is envisaged in concrete terms, and the rather weaker relationship between a ‘precursory' work which, undertaken as an end in itself, subsequently turns out to be ancestral to some later work, which was not specifically envisaged at the time of its production. While, in practice, there may be a shading-off between the ‘preparatory sketch' and the ‘precursor' of a subsequent work, they may, none the less, be opposed as ideal types. Similarly, we may oppose the ‘artist's replica' (like the later version of the Virgin of the Rocks) which is produced with the idea of specifically replicating a previous work, with the unintentional replication of previous works which is a necessary feature of the origination of new works; that is, the painter, intending to produce new work, reproduces his previous work because stylistic coherence and painterly praxis (deeply ingrained artistic habits) demand it. Once again, in reality, there is a shading-off between intentional replication and unintentional recapitulation, but the ideal-typical distinction may be allowed to stand.

zh: 因此，我们可以区分作品之间两种相对“强”的时间关系与两种相对“弱”的时间关系。“强”关系存在于未来或前瞻取向中，即“准备性草图”与完成作品之间；而在此取向中，“弱”关系存在于“先驱”作品（一个并未事先作为系列规划的系列中的第一件）与同系列后续作品之间。相反，在过去或回顾取向中，“强”关系存在于（过去的）原作与随后意图复制这件过去作品的摹本之间；而“弱”关系存在于“原初”作品与随后回归它、修改它、进一步发展它的作品之间——后者在风格逐步变化的过程中重现前作的某些部分。
en: Thus, we may distinguish two relatively ‘strong' temporal relationships between works and two relatively ‘weak' ones. The ‘strong' relationship subsists, in the future, or prospective, orientation, between the ‘preparatory sketch' and the finished work, while, in this orientation, the ‘weak' relation is between the ‘precursory' work (the first in a series which was not planned in advance as a series) and subsequent works in the same series. Conversely, in the past, or retrospective orientation, the ‘strong' relationship subsists between the (past) original and the subsequent copy, which is intended to replicate this past work, while the ‘weak' relationship subsists between the ‘original' work which -through a process of stylistic evolution in which not everything changes all at once is partially recapitulated in subsequent work which returns to it, modifies it, and develops it further.

zh: 现在我们已具备技术概念，可以尝试把艺术家全集作为一个分布式对象——特别是作为时间中的分布式对象——的一般模型，因为艺术家全集在空间中的分布虽是一个有趣的历史问题，却与这里的论点无关。模型的要素是艺术家“全集”中的每一件作品，它们经由刚才描述的四种关系相互关联。
en: We now have the technical concepts in place to essay a general model of the artist’s œuvre as a distributed object-in particular, as a distributed object in time, since the distribution of the artist’s œuvre in space, though an interesting historical question, is beside the point here. The elements of our model are the separate components of the artist’s total œuvre, that is, the ‘complete works' as individual items, which are mutually related via the four relations just described.

zh: 这些关系，从现在起，将被称为强前摄与弱前摄（用于“前瞻”或未来取向的关系），以及强滞留与弱滞留（用于“回顾”或过去取向的关系）。使用这些特定术语的理由，在接下来介绍胡塞尔的时间意识模型时，就能看出缘由。
en: These relations, from now on, will be called strong and weak protentions for ‘prospective' or future-orientated relations, and strong and weak retentions for ‘retrospective' or past-orientated relations. The reason for using these particular terms will become clear once I introduce Husserl's model of time-consciousness, which I intend to do in a moment.

zh: 让前摄／滞留箭头在按年代排列的作品行（点）上下回环，但那会产生一幅相当难读的图。这幅图的要点只是传达这样一个观念：我们可以在宏观尺度上把艺术家全集想象为一件不可分割的作品，由许多物质索引（作品）构成，却相当于一个单一的时间实体，就像一场由许多转瞬即逝的闪电构成的持续雷暴。艺术家的全集是一个可以说由时间构成的对象；不是物理学中那种作为抽象维度的时间（我在别处讨论过并确实辩护过；参见Gell 1992a），而是柏格森命名为绵延（durée）的那种实体化时间。柏格森式绵延——其模型由被视为合目的过程而非随机偶然突变累积的生物进化提供——对物理学家没有意义，但这不是说绵延作为概念没有心理学或认知有效性。的确，有充分理由认为，从认知上理解的人格与主观时间经验同延。把一个人称为“意识”的拥有者，就是指向沿绵延轴按时间排列的一系列认知。但这里我们触及问题的关键。构成艺术家全集的按年代排列的作品集是一组物质对象；它们不是一个人或一组主观经验（认知状态）。它们构成一组索引，从中可以溯因出艺术家的人格与能动性，如前所述（9.2节）。但同时我们很容易设想，“记得”过去发生的某事非常像“复制”一幅自己过去画过的画，或者“为一幅画作初步草图”非常像在心理上预期某个未来事件或行动过程。
en: with the protention/retention arrows looping over and under the row of chronologically arranged works (dots), but that would have resulted in rather an illegible diagram. The point of this diagram is simply to communicate the idea that we can imagine the artist’s œuvre, at the macro-scale, as one indivisible work, consisting of many physical indexes (works) but amounting to a single temporal entity, like a persistent thunderstorm which is made up of many, quasi-instantaneous, flashes of lightning. The artist’s œuvre is an object which, so to speak, is made out of time; not the tenuous, dimensional time of physics (which I have discussed, and indeed defended, elsewhere; cf. Gell 1992a) but the kind of substantialized time which Bergson named durée. Bergsonian durée, a model for which is provided by biological evolution regarded as a teleonomic process rather than as a random accumulation of chance mutations, has no significance for the physicist, but that is not to say that durée has no psychological or cognitive validity as a concept. Indeed, there is every reason to think that personhood, understood cognitively, is coextensive with subjective temporal experience. To refer to a person as a possessor of ‘consciousness' is to refer to a series of cognitions arranged temporally along an axis of durée. But here we reach the crux of the matter. The chronologically arranged set of works which comprise an artist’s œuvre are a set of material objects; they are not a person or a set of subjective experiences (cognitive states). They comprise a set of indexes from which the artist's personhood and agency can be abducted, as was described earlier (Sect. 9.2). But at the same time we can easily conceive that ‘remembering' something which happened in the past is very like ‘copying' a picture that one has painted in the past, or that ‘making a preliminary sketch for a picture' is very like mentally anticipating some future happening or course of action.

zh: 换言之，艺术家全集中个别作品的安排——每件都部分是先前作品的重演、部分是尚未开始作品的预期——似乎让全集里的索引（外部世界中的对象）彼此发生联系，就像心智状态在我们称为意识的认知过程中彼此发生联系一样。换言之，艺术家全集中索引对索引关系的时间结构，外在化或客观化了与艺术家作为赋有意识的存在其内部心智状态之间存在的关系相同的类型。艺术家的全集把创作意识（认知和时间意义上的人格）放大，使它公开，也让人得以接触。
en: In other words, the arrangement of individual works in an artist’s œuvre, each of which is partly a recapitulation of previous works and partly an anticipation of works as yet uncommenced, seems to generate the same kind of relationships between indexes (which are objects in the external world) as exist between mental states in the cognitive process we recognize as consciousness. In other words, the temporal structure of index-to-index relations in the artist’s œuvre externalizes or objectifies the same type of relations as exist between the artist's internal states of mind as a being endowed with consciousness. The artist’s œuvre is artistic consciousness (personhood in the cognitive, temporal sense) writ large and rendered public and accessible.

zh: 但“认知”发生在哪里？——在艺术家头脑中，还是在他的画布上？当然，任何心智的认知过程，尤其贯穿整段生命历程，大多是不可接近的私人经验，只留下最难以辨认的痕迹。而且我们几乎无法把艺术家全集聚合为一个统一的“时间对象”，除非每件个别作品都曾在某一阶段起源于艺术家心智中制作某个特定的索引的意图（即一种产生艺术能动性的心智状态）。但我们前面简要考察过的关于创造性能动性的生成—检验模型最清楚地揭示，“思考”既发生在我们之内也发生在我们之外。诗人写下诗行，然后划掉，借助落在纸上的文字修改、推敲诗句。这些文字是先前心智活动留下的物质痕迹。图形艺术家尤为如此。他不断从先前的作品中得到启发，推动新的创作，也在创作中自由修改。更一般地说，艺术家生活在自己作品的包围中，完成的或半完成的，它们散乱在画室，为他提供多年来活动的常在记录（对那些作品找不到买家的艺术家来说，也许是其全部活动）。
en: But where does ‘cognition' take place?-in the artist's head, or on his canvases? Mostly, of course, the cognitive processes of any mind, especially over a whole biographical career, are inaccessible private experiences which leave only the most indecipherable traces. And we could hardly aggregate an artist’s œuvre as a unified ‘temporal object' unless each of the individual works had, at one stage, originated as an intention in the artist's mind to produce such and such an index (i.e. a state of mind giving rise to artistic agency). But the generate-and-test model of creative agency, which we briefly examined earlier on, reveals most clearly that ‘thinking' takes place outside us as well as inside us. The poet writes down his lines, and then scratches them out, altering and improving his verses in ways that crucially depend on the existence of physical traces of his previous (mental) activity. And this is still truer of the graphic artist, who continually uses his own past production as a spur to his future production, altering and modifying freely as he goes along. And in more general terms, the artist lives surrounded by his own works, completed or half-completed, which litter the studio and provide him with an ever-present record of his activity over many years (maybe all his activity in the case of artists whose works find no buyers).

zh: 艺术家的全集可以这样理解：每一件作品都是先前作品的一次变样、一次修订，是贯穿生涯的生成—检验序列中某一轮创作留下的成果。诚然，这个模型有些理想化，艺术的大部分由常规产出构成，而非追求完美的结果。但更有创造性、历史上更重要的艺术家确实以这种方式发展，他们的作品可以被读作一个累积的发现过程，而非仅仅对早年学会、从未忘记、也从未超越的技术程序的利用。
en: The artist’s œuvre can be understood like this; each separate work is a modification, a recension, of previous ones, the leftovers of a particular cycle in a career-long generate-and-test sequence. To be sure, this model is somewhat idealized, and much of art consists of routine output rather than the results of strivings after perfection. But the more inventive and historically important artists do develop in this way, and their work can be read as a cumulative process of discovery rather than the mere exploitation of technical procedures learnt early, never forgotten, and never surpassed.

zh: 我想从创造性的“生成—检验”模型中进一步引出的概念是变样。对熟悉认知哲学文献的人来说，这个词会令人感到耳熟，因为它是胡塞尔（在英译中）使用的词，他把“变样”（形象、知觉，即思想对象的变样）概念置于核心位置，以此说明意识怎样在时间中展开。我在一部先前著作中已提供对胡塞尔“内在时间意识”模型的说明，我打算在这里重述我对胡塞尔模型的某些评论。我这样做的理由是，胡塞尔模型能帮助我们澄清前面几页所呈现的艺术家全集作为时间对象（或也许应说“跨时间对象”）模型的某些特征。特别是，它将帮助我们摆脱一个我尚未揭示的严重矛盾。
en: The concept that I want to draw out further from the ‘generate-and-test' model of creativity is that of modification. For one versed in the philosophical literature of cognition this word rings bells, because it is a word used (in English translations) by Husserl, who assigns the concept of ‘modification' (of images, perceptions, i.e. the objects of thought) a central role in his model of consciousness as a temporal process. I have provided an account of Husserl's model of ‘internal time-consciousness' in a previous work, and I propose to recapitulate some of my comments on Husserl's model here. My reason for doing so is that Husserl's model can help us to clarify certain features of the model of the artist’s œuvre as a temporal object (or perhaps one should say, as a ‘trans-temporal object') that has been presented in the preceding pages. In particular, it will help us to escape from a serious contradiction that I have not yet brought to light.

zh: 假设我们有两件作品X与Y，使得X是对Y的“弱前摄”，即X可以被看作Y的先驱，但不是明确的“为Y的习作”。现在，当X正在被绘制的过程中，Y在具体意义上未被画家或任何其他人设想。所能说的只是，画家在从事X时“希望”画未来的画，这些画可能在技术与主题上与X相关，但他对“下一幅”画是什么只有模糊的直觉。Y仍然（且只是）一幅设想中的“未来”画作，现实中还找不到它。最终，画家会着手画他的下一幅画（比方说系列中的下一件），结果它就是Y。现在我们有了X与Y，而之前只有X。审视Y时，我们（和画家）能够看到Y在许多方面在X中被预显，并在此基础上倾向于说Y重演X，Y是X的“弱滞留”，因为X作为Y的“初步版本”被滞留在Y中。但等等，这里有个问题，因为我们已经假设（以模糊而非具体的方式）Y从X被前摄，即就艺术家的发展而言Y可见地是X所前摄者。Y怎么可能同时既是从X被前摄（作为尚未实现的“未来”画），又在Y实际存在之后“滞留”X作为一种记忆痕迹？当这两个Y似乎具有矛盾属性时，我们怎样把由X前摄到的“Y”与保留了X痕迹的Y认作同一件作品；即Y能否在同一时刻既是从X的前摄又是X的滞留？这似乎涉及某种逻辑冲突，然而当我们思考艺术家全集中作品之间的关系时，我们想两全其美；我们想看到后来的画在先前的画中被“预显”，又想看到后来的画中有先前画的“痕迹”或记忆。时间上分离的画之间这两种关系显然不同，然而当我们把它们放在一起时，它们似乎以最令人困惑的方式混在一起，难以区分。
en: Suppose we have two works, X and Y, such that X is a ‘weak protention' towards Y, that is that X can be seen as a precursor of Y but not as a definite ‘study for' Y. Now, while X is in the process of being painted, Y is unimagined by the painter or by anybody else, in concrete terms. All that one can say is that the painter, while engaged on X, ‘hopes' to paint future paintings, which will probably be related, technically and thematically, to X, but he only has a vague intuition as to what his ‘next' picture will be. Y is still (and only) a ‘future' painting, nothing in the world corresponds to it. Eventually, the painter will get round to painting his next picture (let us say, the next in a series) and it turns out to be Y. Now we have both X and Y whereas before we only had X. On inspecting Y we (and the painter) are able to see that Y was prefigured in X in very many respects, and, on this basis, we are inclined to say that Y recapitulates X, that Y is a ‘weak retention' of X in that X is retained in Y as a ‘preliminary version' of Y. But wait, there is a problem here, because we have already supposed that (in vague, if not specific, terms) Y has been protended from X, that is, Y is visibly what X protends in terms of the artist's development. How can it be simultaneously the case that Y is protended from X (as a not-yet-realized ‘future' painting) and simultaneously that Y ‘retains' X as a kind of memory-trace now that Y has actually come into existence. How can we identify the ‘Y' which was a protention from X and the Y which is a retention of X, when it would appear that these two Ys have contradictory properties; that is, can Y be a protention from X and a retention of X, at one and the same moment? This seems to involve some kind of logical conflict, yet, when we think about the relations between works of art in an artist's oeuvre, we want to have it both ways; we want to see later pictures ‘prefigured' in earlier ones, and we want to see ‘traces' or memories of earlier pictures in later ones. These two types of relation between temporally separated pictures are clearly not the same, yet when we place them together they seem to collapse into one another in a most confusing way.

zh: 如果你愿意，这是时间哲学中一个熟悉困境的艺术史版本——事件与时态的问题。让我用一个例子解释。我约了明天看医生。我今天把这个事件前摄为一个将（可能）发生的未来事件，但我不知道例如医生会说什么或他会推荐什么治疗。到后天，这次约诊将是一个过去事件（我将对它有记忆或滞留），它曾短暂地是一个“现在”事件（明天）。显然，无论今天是“今天”（1996年10月15日）、还是昨天、上周、明天、后天、或你喜欢的任何日子，这个事件（预约）都是“同一个事件”。然而这个唯一事件在这些不同日子具有现在性、过去性、未来性的矛盾属性；“一个事件”怎么能既是过去又是现在又是未来而不产生矛盾？
en: This, if you like, is the art-historical version of a familiar dilemma in the philosophy of time-the problem of events and tenses. Let me explain this by means of an example. Tomorrow I have a doctor's appointment. I protend this event, today, as a future event which will (probably) transpire, but I do not know, for instance, what the doctor will say or what treatment he will recommend. By the day after tomorrow, tomorrow's doctor's appointment will be a past event (of which I will have a memory, or retention) having transiently been a ‘present' event (tomorrow). Obviously, this event (the appointment) is the ‘same event' whether today is ‘today' (15 October 1996), or yesterday, or last week, or tomorrow, or the day after tomorrow, or whatever day you please. Yet this unique event, on these various days, has the contradictory properties of presentness, pastness, or futurity; and how can ‘one event' be past and present and future, without contradiction arising?

zh: 这个谜题的答案显然是，像约诊这样先被预期、继而发生、随后成为过去的事件，并不以一劳永逸的方式拥有过去性、现在性、未来性的属性，而只是短暂地拥有，取决于我们从某个不断移动的“现在”时刻对有关事件所持的“观点”。未来事件的“未来”性质当然影响我们看待它的方式（用语法学家的术语说，它有一种非现实色彩），但即便如此，我们毫不困难地把一个仅被“预期”的未来事件，与（或多或少）对应我们预期而实际发生的事件，以及当它滑回过去成为“单纯记忆”时以相当不同方式变为非现实的对该事件的记忆，识别为同一。同一个事件，作为可能的未来事件、作为正在被经验的现在事件、作为可被回忆的过去事件，仍是一个事件，但随着我们对它的时间视角移动，该事件从认知主体的立场经历一系列变样。它透过未来与过去时间的各种厚度被观看，这些厚度改变它的外观，可以说改变它的时间包浆。
en: The answer to this puzzle is obviously that events like doctors' appointments, which are anticipated in advance, become present, and fall away into the past, do not possess attributes of pastness, presentness, and futurity in a once-and-for-all way, but only transiently, depending on the ‘point of view' we have on the event in question from a certain ‘now' moment, which continually shifts. The ‘future' quality of a future event certainly colours our attitude to it (it has an irrealis shading, to use the grammarians' term), but even so we have no difficulty in identifying a future event which was only ‘anticipated' with the event corresponding to our anticipations (more or less) which actually does happen, and the memory of that event which becomes irrealis in a rather different way as it slips back into the past and becomes a ‘mere memory'. The same event, as a possible future event, as a present event which is being experienced, and as a past event which can be recalled, remains one event, but as our temporal perspective on this event shifts, the event undergoes a series of modifications from the standpoint of the cognitive subject. It is seen through various thicknesses of future and past time, which alter its appearance, its temporal patination, so to speak.

zh: 胡塞尔在其职业生涯初期研究这一问题，当时他有兴趣描述一般认知过程，以便（最终）能够把关于认知的“心理学”事实与先验哲学确定性分开，他提出了一个非常有用的“时间意识”模型。它旨在描绘“意向对象”（noemata，认知对象）怎样随一个个“现在”时刻的流逝而有规律地变样，也就是怎样随着主体时间视角的移动而变化。
en: Husserl, working on this problem towards the beginning of his career, when he was interested in describing cognitive processes in general so as to be able (eventually) to separate ‘psychological' facts about cognition from transcendental philosophical certainties, put forward a most useful model of ‘time-consciousness’. This is designed to depict the systematic modification of the ‘noemata' (the objects of cognition) as a function of the passage of successive ‘now' moments, that is, shifts in the subject's time-perspective.

zh: 为阐述其观念，胡塞尔使用一幅图，
（来自Gell 1992a）是其一个版本。水平线A→B→C→D对应于在过去与未来之间串起的“现在”时刻发生的事件或“事态”的相继。假定当下是B，知觉也更新到了B。B处的时间景观由对B处事态正在发生的知觉经验，加上A的滞留（作为A′，逐渐淡入过去性）构成。A′（从B看的A）是原初A的一次变样——A从B“看起来”的样子，即被衰减或减弱，但仍与现在相连。也许可以把A沉入过去（在
上向左下对角）时的“变样”（A→A′→A″→A‴…）理解为一种逐渐丧失逼真性的过程，影响A处的知觉，因为它渐渐被B、C、D等处的知觉取代。我们对任一“现在”时刻事态的知觉不会立即变得不适用，而只是逐渐地，因为世界不会一下子在所有方面改变。在B处我们不再能说A处的事态“现在”如此，因为时间视角改变了；但A的许多特征在B处有对应物，B的特征在C处有对应物，如此等等。
en: In order to expound his ideas, Husserl makes use of a diagram, of which

(from Gell 1992a) is a version. The horizontal line A → B → C → D corresponds to the succession of events or ‘states of affairs' occurring at ‘now' moments strung out between the past and the future. Suppose we are at B: our perceptions up to date at B. The temporal landscape at B consists of the now-present perceptual experience of the state of affairs at B plus retentions of A, as A', shading away into pastness. A' (A seen from B) is a modification of the original A-what A ‘looks like' from B, that is, attenuated or diminished, but still connected to the present. Perhaps one can think of the ‘modification' of A as it sinks (diagonally to the left on

) down into the past (A → A′ → A″ → A‴ … ) as a gradual loss of verisimilitude affecting the perceptions entertained at A as these are superseded by the perceptions entertained at B, C, D, etc. Our perceptions of the state of affairs as it is at any one ‘now' moment do not become inapplicable immediately, but only gradually, because the world does not change all at once and in all respects. We can no longer, at B, say that the state of affairs at A is ‘now' the case, because of the change of temporal perspective; but many of the features of A have counterparts at B, and features of B have counterparts at C, and so on.
