zh: 滞留因此可以被理解为过时知觉的背景，较新的知觉投射其上，并校准显著趋势与变化。随着时间拉长、知觉越来越陈旧，它们的显著性降低并消失于视野。因此我们知觉现在不是作为一个刀锋般的“现在”，而是作为一个时间上延展的场，在其中趋势从我们在对邻近过去、次邻近过去、再下一个过去等等的知觉相继更新中所辨识的模式中涌现。这一趋势以前摄的形式投射到未来，即对当前知觉更新模式的预期，这些更新将在邻近未来、次邻近未来、再下一个未来成为必需，以与过去对称但时间顺序相反的方式。
en: Retentions can thus be construed as the background of out-of-date perceptions against which more up-to-date perceptions are projected, and significant trends and changes are calibrated. As perceptions become more seriously out of date, they diminish in salience and are lost to view. We thus perceive the present not as a knife-edge ‘now' but as a temporally extended field within which trends emerge out of the patterns we discern in the successive updatings of perceptions relating to the proximate past, the next more proximate past, and the next, and so on. This trend is projected into the future in the form of protentions, that is, anticipations of the pattern of updating of current perceptions which will be necessitated in the proximate future, the next most proximate future, and the next, in a manner symmetric with the past, but in inverse temporal order.

zh: 让我们继续胡塞尔本人对其模型的解释。在B处，A被滞留为A′（透过某种时间厚度看的A），C被前摄为C′，即人们认为在B之后最可能发生的事。时间流逝，C′作为C到来（大概不完全如预期，但大致如此）。B现在在意识中被滞留为B′，与（当前）C的关系如同B当前时A′与B的关系。但A与C如何关联？从C的立场，A不再被滞留为A′，因为那会把A′与B′等量齐观，未能反映这样一个事实：当B（如今的B′）还在当下时，A即使在那时也只是一个滞留（A′）。因此，从C的立场，A必须被滞留为A′的滞留，而A′本身是A的滞留：即作为A″。
en: Let us continue with Husserl’s own explanation of his model. At B, A is retained as A′ (A seen through a certain thickness of time) and C is protended as C′, the favoured candidate as successor to B. Time passes, and C′ comes about as C (presumably not quite as anticipated, but approximately so). B is now retained in consciousness as B′, related to (current) C as A′ was to B when B was current. But how is A related to C? From the standpoint of C, A is no longer retained as A′, because this is to put A′ and B′ on a par with one another, and fails to reflect the fact that when B (currently B′) was current, A was even then only a retention (A′). Consequently, from the standpoint of C, A has to be retained as a retention of A′, which is itself a retention of A: that is, as A″.

zh: 胡塞尔说，当在B处，A下沉为A′，到C处下沉为A″，到D处下沉为A‴，等等，一个知觉变成滞留，然后变成滞留的滞留，然后变成滞留的滞留的滞留，等等，直到达到最终衰减并沉到时间地平线之下的阶段。这一论证的效果是废除动态现在与固定不变过去之间的僵硬区分。过去、现在、未来在胡塞尔模型中都是一体的、同样动态的（体现一个重要的认知真理），因为系统中任何地方的任何变样都会在系统其他所有地方引起相关变样。因此当下把C转化为C′的变样

自动带动各处相应的变样（B′ → B″、A″ → A‴、D′ → D，等等）。“整个过去连同其中一切排定的内容一同下沉”（Findlay 1975: 11）。但过去不只是随着现在推进而“下沉”；它改变其意义，被以不同方式评价，并根据现在演进的方式建立不同的前摄模式。这种动态的过去、以及不断改变面貌的未来，只能在认知时间中得到说明，单凭“物理”时间无法解释。在提供其滞留、前摄、变样等模型时，胡塞尔不是在描述一个当事件从未来浮现、在现在实现自身、沉入过去时发生在事件上的神秘物理过程，而是在描述连接经验主体与他所经验的以现在为中心的世界的意向性的变化光谱。“变样”不是A本身的变化，而是随着随后经验累积我们对A的看法的变化。
en: Husserl says that as A sinks to A′ at B, A″ at C, A‴ at D, and so on, a perception becomes a retention, then a retention of a retention, then a retention of a retention of a retention, and so on, until reaching the stage of final attenuation and sinking beneath the temporal horizon. The effect of this argument is to abolish the hard-and-fast distinction between the dynamic present and the fixed and unchanging past. Past, present, and future are all of a piece, and all equally dynamic in the Husserl model (embodying an important cognitive truth) because any modification, anywhere in the system, sets up correlative modifications everywhere else in the system. Thus the modification in the present which converts C into C′ automatically entrains corresponding modifications everywhere (B′ → B″, A″ → A‴, D′ → D, etc.). ‘The whole past sinks in a mass, taking all its arranged contents with it' (Findlay 1975: 11). But the past does not just ‘sink' as the present progresses; it changes its significance, is evaluated in different ways, and sets up different patterns of protentions, according to the way in which the present evolves. This dynamic past, and the future which continually alters in complexion, cannot be accommodated in ‘physical' time, but only in cognitive time. In providing his model of retentions, protentions, modifications, etc., Husserl is not describing an arcane physical process which occurs to events as they loom out of the future, actualize themselves in the present, and sink into the past, but is describing the changing spectrum of intentionalities linking the experiencing subject and the present-focused world which he experiences. ‘Modification' is not a change in A itself, but a change in our view of A as the result of subsequent accretions of experience.

zh: 胡塞尔在以下段落中总结他对内在时间意识的看法：
en: Husserl summarizes his view of internal time-consciousness in the following passage:

zh: 意识中每一个现实的“现在”都服从变样规律。它变为滞留的滞留，并且连续地如此。于是产生一个滞留的规则连续统，使得每个较后的点都是每个较前点的滞留。每个滞留本身已是一个连续统。一个音开始并稳定持续：它的当下阶段变为刚过去的阶段，我们的印象意识不断流入一个常新的滞留意识。顺流而下，我们遇到一个连续系列的滞留，回溯到起点。对每个这样的滞留，附加一个滞留变样的连续统，而这个连续统本身又是正在被滞留投射的现实中的一个点……每个滞留内在地是一个连续变样，可以说在自身中携带其过去的遗产。不仅顺流而下每个较前的滞留被一个新的连续替换。每个较后的滞留不仅是源于原初印象的连续变样：它也是同一起点的所有先前连续变样的连续变样。（1928: 390，引自Findlay 1975: 10）
en: Every actual Now of consciousness is subject to the law of modification. It changes into the retention of a retention and does so continuously. There accordingly arises a regular continuum of retention such that every later point is the retention of every earlier one. Each retention is already a continuum. A tone begins and goes on steadily: its now-phase changes into a was-phase, and our impressional consciousness constantly flows over into an ever new retentional consciousness. Going down the stream, we encounter a continuous series of retentions harking back to the starting point. To each of such retentions a continuum of retentional modifications is added, and this continuum is itself a point in the actuality that is being retentionally projected ... Each retention is intrinsically a continuous modification, which so to say carries the heritage of its past in itself. It is not merely the case, that, going downstream, each earlier retention is continuously replaced by a new one. Each later retention is not merely a continuous modification stemming from an original impression: it is also a continuous modification of all previous continuous modifications of the same starting point. (1928: 390, cited in Findlay 1975: 10)

zh: 同样，未来事件并不真的“改变”，尽管从我们的观点看它们变得不那么不确定、更迫近，并且随着接近可以越来越精确地预期。但我们有一种很自然地会这样看它们。胡塞尔模型经由前摄变样的连续统的连续统处理这一点。前摄是当下根据它似乎所属的那个时间整体而作的向前延伸：“不完全地、且在其发展中意识到一个发展中的整体，却总是意识到它作为一个整体：尚未写入的，被写入为尚待写入”（Findlay 1975: 9）。
en: Similarly, future events, do not really ‘change' as a result of the fact that, from our point of view, they are becoming less indefinite, more imminent, and can be anticipated with increasing degrees of precision as they approach. But we have a strong compulsion to view them in such a light. Husserl's model treats this via a continuum of continua of protentional modifications. Protentions are continuations of the present in the light of the kind of temporal whole the present seems to belong to: ‘To be aware of a developing whole incompletely, and as it develops, is yet always to be aware of it as a whole: what is not yet written in, is written in as yet to be written in’ (Findlay 1975: 9).

zh: 胡塞尔模型中的A、B、C对应于“事件”或事态。我想建议的是，它们可以被替换为作为艺术家全集构成成分的个别艺术作品。这些是物质对象而非“事件”，但尽管如此，它们是事件的痕迹或索引，即使其成为物质对象的事件或创作行为。我主张的是，要把艺术家全集理解为一个统一的时间对象，也要遵循同样的“变样规律”。这意味着，我们不能把艺术家全集看作时间对象，除非我们选择某一件特定作品对应于一个“现在”时刻，并把全集中所有其他作品看作相对于由我们选作时间立足点的特定作品所定义的“现在”的“过去”或“未来”作品。
en: The As and Bs and Cs in Husserl's model correspond to ‘events' or states of affairs. What I want to suggest is that they can be replaced by individual works of art as constituents of an artist’s œuvre. These are physical objects rather than ‘events', but, all the same, they are traces or indexes of events, that is, the events or performances which brought them physically into being. What I am arguing is that if one seeks to construct the artist’s œuvre as a unified temporal object, the same basic ‘law of modifications' applies. What this means is that we cannot see the artist’s œuvre as a temporal object except on condition that we select one particular work as corresponding to a ‘now' moment, and see all the other works in the œuvre as either ‘past' or ‘future' works in relation to the ‘now' defined by the particular work that we have selected as our temporal vantage-point.

zh: 因此，回到我们前面的讨论，我们只有把自己置于Y尚不存在的时间立足点，才能把较早的画X看作Y的“先驱”（从X对Y的前摄）；相反，我们只有把立足点移到一个Y已存在、X是“过去”作品的较后“现在”，才能把Y看作X的重演（X的滞留）。我们不能同时占据这两个立足点。这等于说我们不能从永恒的视角（sub specie aeternitatis）把艺术家全集当作一个完整的时间对象来看。我们所能做的只是编纂一份关于全集整体的不同时间视角的“档案”。
en: Thus, to return to our previous discussion, we can only see an earlier painting, X, as a ‘precursor' of Y (protention of Y from X) by situating ourselves at a vantage-point in time at which Y does not yet exist, and conversely, we can only see Y as a recapitulation of X (a retention of X) by shifting our point of vantage to a later ‘now' at which Y has come into existence, and X is a ‘past' work. We cannot occupy both of these vantage-points at the same time. This is the same as saying that we cannot totalize an artist’s œuvre as a temporal object which can be regarded sub specie aeternitatis. All we can do is compile a ‘file' of different temporal perspectives on the œuvre as a whole.

zh: 假设一位艺术家在其生涯中创作500件作品，我们可以编号Op.1到Op.500。我们可以“从第1件作品出发”（即作为从Op.1出发的一组非常模糊的前摄）、或从生涯中期（从Op.250出发的前摄与滞留）、或从“最后作品”（从Op.500出发的滞留，以及朝向我们只能想象、艺术家若活得更久可能完成的作品的前摄）构建艺术家全集。我主张，取决于我们取哪个作品编号作为立足点，我们所见的前摄与滞留关系便各有一种格局，从而获得对艺术家全集的不同解释。没有任何绝对意义可以把任何给定作品看作先前作品的重演或未来作品的先驱；艺术家在时间中串起的作品整体构成一个动态、不稳定的实体，而非可断代人工制品的单纯累积。我们只有参与其展开的生命才能领会它。
en: Suppose an artist creates, in the course of his career, 500 works which we can number Op. 1 through to Op. 500. We can construct the artist’s œuvre ‘from the standpoint of Op. 1’ (i.e. as a very vague set of protentions from Op. 1), or from mid-career (protentions and retentions from Op. 250), or from ‘last works' (retentions from Op. 500 and protentions towards works which we can only imagine, which the artist might have completed had he lived longer). Depending on which opus number we take as our point of vantage, I would argue, we obtain a different, unique, patterning of protentional and retentional relationships between works, and thus a different interpretation of the artist’s œuvre. There is no absolute sense in which any given work can be seen, either as a recapitulation of a previous work, or as a precursor of a future one; the ensemble of an artist's works, strung out in time, constitutes a dynamic, unstable, entity; not a mere accumulation of datable artefacts. We can only appreciate it by participating in its unfolding life.

zh: 读者此时可能反对：“这都很好，可再怎么想，我也很难把你说的同任何一位我熟悉的艺术家的全部作品联系起来——比如卡纳莱托”。我将不得不承认，卡纳莱托的城市景观，尽管令人钦佩，似乎很难被解释为心理学文献，而非地形学文献。我一直推进的模型最适用于其全集体现高度有意识自我指涉与连贯发展的艺术家。我远非声称刚才推进的模型在所有艺术史语境中都特别有用。然而，该模型可以容易地至少在某些历史语境中应用，我现在就转向其中之一。
en: The reader may object at this point; ‘this is all very well, but try as I may I find it hard to connect what you are saying to the actual œuvre of any artist whose works I know-Canaletto for instance'. And I would be obliged to admit that Canaletto's cityscapes, admirable though they are, hardly seem amenable to interpretation as psychological documents, as opposed to topographical ones. The model I have been advancing best applies to artists whose œuvre embodies a high degree of conscious self-reference and coherent development. I am far from claiming that the model just advanced would be particularly useful in all art-historical contexts. However, the model can easily be made to apply in at least some historical contexts, and it is to one of these I shall now turn.

zh: 9.5　马塞尔·杜尚的作品全集
en: 9.5　The Œuvre of Marcel Duchamp

zh: 从某种意义上说，接下来我要取个巧。胡塞尔的时间意识模型源于这样一个时期：时空、连续性、物理实在与心智状态之间的关系等问题非常“流行”。他对这一主题的处理明显带有威廉·詹姆斯的影响，而另一位处理这些问题的同时代哲学家——他可能对艺术史进程施加了某种直接影响——是亨利·柏格森。分析立体主义的诞生、胡塞尔《内在时间意识心理学》的出现、柏格森最广为阅读的著作《创造进化论》的出版，几乎是同时的事件（1906与1907年间）。我将用其作品来例证我论点的艺术家马塞尔·杜尚，恰恰在这一时期经历了塑造他思想的那段时期。虽然杜尚从未系统学习哲学或数学，他却轻易拾取了年轻时智识圈中流传的观念。此外，他阅读并掌握了一些普及高等数学与科学思维的文本（尤其是庞加莱与茹弗雷；见Adcock 1984）。因此，尽管观念的实际扩散可能永远无法被记录——我当然不打算记录它——事实是杜尚可能在某种程度上意识到（即使只是间接地、经由立体主义者（及其圈内哲学家普林塞））詹姆斯—柏格森—胡塞尔的时间流变或“意识流”观念。因此用杜尚来例证一个“胡塞尔式”艺术史模型可能涉及某种同义反复，因为事实上杜尚可能本来就着手去例证它。
en: In a sense, I am going to cheat. Husserl’s model of time-consciousness dates from a period in which problems of space-time, continuity, and the relation between physical reality and mental states were very much ‘in the air'. His treatment of the subject shows, markedly, the influence of William James, while another contemporary philosopher who tackled these problems--and who may have exercised some direct influence on the course of art history - was Henri Bergson. The birth of analytical Cubism, the appearance of Husserl's Psychology of Internal Time Consciousness, and the publication of Bergson's most widely read work Creative Evolution were almost simultaneous events (between 1906 and 1907). The artist whose work I am going to use to illustrate my thesis, Marcel Duchamp, underwent his formative intellectual experiences during precisely this period. Though Duchamp never studied philosophy or mathematics systematically, he readily picked up the ideas that were doing the rounds in intellectual circles in his youth. Moreover, he read and mastered a number of texts (notably by Poincaré and Jouffret; see Adcock 1984) which popularized advanced mathematical and scientific thinking. Consequently, although the actual diffusion of ideas might never be documentable -and I certainly do not intend to document it-the fact is that Duchamp was probably to some extent aware, even if only indirectly, via the Cubists (and their in-house philosopher, Princet) of the James-Bergson-Husserl conception of temporal flux or the ‘stream of consciousness'. So there might be an element of tautology involved in using Duchamp to illustrate a 'Husserlian' model of art history, when, in fact, Duchamp may actually have set out to illustrate it.

zh: 无论如何，杜尚无疑提供了迄今为止最清晰的实例：一位重要艺术家，其全部作品值得作为从特定作品（特别是从其杰作《新娘甚至被她的单身汉们剥光》——亦即《大玻璃》（1913-25））扇形展开的前摄与滞留网络来研究。显然，我在这里只能暗示杜尚全集的丰富性，那需要一部专著来补充已存在的关于这位艺术家的众多专著，其中某些充分记录了我在这里探索的基本观念（尤其见C. E. Adcock 1984的著作）。
en: However that may be, Duchamp certainly provides by far the most perspicuous instance of an important artist whose total œuvre repays study as a network of protentions and retentions fanning out from particular works (particularly from his masterpiece La Mariée mise à nu par les célibataires, même—otherwise known as The Large Glass (1913-25)). I cannot, obviously, do more than hint at the richness of Duchamp’s œuvre here—that would require a monograph to add to the many that already exist on this artist, certain of which copiously document the basic idea I am exploring here (see, especially, the work of C. E. Adcock 1984).

zh: 杜尚的作品本质上是关于连续统观念的，因为它基于对“第四维”观念的利用。我应当立即说，这一维度不是普通意义上的“时间”，尤其不是作为单纯持续时间度量的时间，或物理学家的时间。对杜尚——以及对他某些同时代人——而言，“第四维”本质上是超出或包容我们日常生活和感知的“普通”世界的、“真实”但严格不可表象的领域。杜尚的作品起源于一则数学家的寓言。一个二维对象（在平面中，如在阿博特著名的《平面国》中）投下一维的影子。一个三维对象（我们在三维世界中熟悉的那种对象）投下二维的影子。那么什么样的对象会投下三维的影子？——显然，那必须是一个“四维对象”；因此它是某种可以设想但无法再现的东西，因为要表象它需要比我们在三维之地所能支配的更多的维度。杜尚的艺术，彻底简化地说，由一系列本质上喜剧性的尝试构成：生产四维实体的“影子”，或至少通过外推三维对象的影子来暗示获得这些四维对象影子的程序。
en: Duchamp's work is, essentially, about the notion of the continuum, in that it is based on the exploitation of the idea of the ‘fourth dimension’. This dimension, I should immediately say, is not ‘time' in the ordinary sense, especially not time as a mere measure of duration, or physicists' time. The ‘fourth dimension' for Duchamp-as for certain of his contemporaries-was essentially the ‘real' but strictly unrepresentable domain beyond, or encompassing, the 'ordinary' world we live in and perceive in the normal way. Duchamp's work originates in a mathematician's parable. A two-dimensional object (in the plane, e.g. in Abbot's famous Flatland) casts a one-dimensional shadow. A three-dimensional object (the kind of object we are familiar with in our 3-d world) casts a two-dimensional shadow. So what kind of object would cast a three-dimensional shadow?-obviously, that would have to be a ‘fourth-dimensional object'; which is thus something which one can conceive of, but not represent, because to do so requires more dimensions than we have at our disposal, here in three-dimensional land. Duchamp's art, to simplify radically, consists of a series of essentially comic attempts to produce ‘shadows' of fourth-dimensional entities, or at least to suggest procedures for obtaining these shadows of fourth-dimensional objects by extrapolating the shadows of three-dimensional ones.

zh: 起初，杜尚只是模糊地把第四维等同于一个象征主义的乌有之乡。1910-11年他创作了一批“象征主义”作品，最后是《春天里的青年与少女》（1911），我们稍后将以不同面貌遇到它。从1911年中起，他开始受到立体主义者的影响。立体主义者对第四维感兴趣，不是作为象征神话而是作为主观经验的事实，在立体主义影响下杜尚的第四维观念越来越接近柏格森的“绵延”。立体主义“经典”阶段的根本意图是创造“写实”的形象，向观者展示对象真实的样子，而非仅仅对象“看起来”的样子。立体主义者所钦佩的较早十九世纪艺术家是“写实主义者”，尤其是库尔贝与柯罗。庸俗公众对立体主义者声称更高“写实主义”是其目标感到困惑，但立体主义者能为其计划引用大量哲学先例。暗示吉他与瓶子可能不止于从固定视点瞬时观看的可见外观，在哲学上并非无先例。把这一洞见转化为艺术实践更困难。塞尚已指明道路，例如在他某些晚期圣维克多山描绘中——正如后来在塞尚架起画架的地点所作的摄影研究将要证明的——这些描绘展示了比从任何一个这些立足点实际所能看到的更多的圣维克多山。这些风景描绘的不是圣维克多山的任何固定外观，而是塞尚随时间同这座山的交互。他在附近走动，将各个角度的所见逐一吸收进来。或换言之，圣维克多山被揭示为一个过程、一场绵延的运动，而非一个“物”。立体主义“多视点”的弱点是它容易退化为一种绘画电影，其中运动对象（或被运动相机观看的对象）的相继“帧”被简单地一张贴一张。立体主义理论家如格莱兹与梅青格尔，孜孜不倦地强调立体主义中的观念论要素，即它对“绝对”的绘画等价物的寻求，而非对动态运动与变化的轻易唤起。另一方面，意大利未来主义者热情拥抱“电影主义”，因为与他们的巴黎立体主义同行不同，他们特别感兴趣于运动与动态现象（如波丘尼）。
en: To begin with, Duchamp merely identified the fourth dimension vaguely with a Symbolist never-never land. In 1910–11 he produced ‘Symbolist' works which culminate in the Young Man and Girl in Spring (1911), which we will encounter in a different guise later. From mid-1911 onwards, he fell under the influence of the Cubists. The Cubists were interested in the fourth dimension, not as a symbolic myth but as a fact of subjective experience, and under Cubist influence Duchamp's notion of the fourth dimension became aligned, more and more, with Bergsonian durée. The underlying intention behind the 'classic' phase of Cubism was to create images which were ‘realistic' in showing the spectator what the object really was like, rather than merely what the object ‘looked' like. The earlier nineteenth-century artists admired by the Cubists were the ‘realists', notably Courbet and Corot. The philistine public was bemused by Cubist claims to the effect that superior ‘realism' was their goal, but the Cubists could cite copious philosophical precedents for their project. It is not philosophically unprecedented to suggest that there could be more to guitars and bottles than their visible appearance, viewed instantaneously and from a fixed point of view. Translating this insight into artistic practice was more difficult. Cézanne had shown the way, for example in some of his late depictions of Mont Sainte-Victoire, which-as later photographic researches at the spots at which Cézanne set up his easel were to prove-showed more of Mont Sainte-Victoire than could ever actually be seen from any one of these vantage-points. These landscapes depict, not any fixed appearance of Mont Sainte-Victoire, but Cezanne's interaction with this object over time, as he moved about in its vicinity and absorbed each of its varied aspects. Or, in other words, Mont Sainte-Victoire is revealed as a process, a movement of durée, rather than as a ‘thing'. The weak point of Cubist ‘multiple perspective' was that it could easily degenerate into a kind of painted cinema, in which successive ‘frames' of a moving object, or an object seen by a moving camera, were simply pasted one on top of another. Cubist theoreticians, such as Gleizes and Metzinger, sedulously sought to emphasize the idealistic element in Cubism, its search for the pictorial equivalent of ‘the absolute' rather than the facile evocation of dynamic motion and change. The Italian Futurists, on the other hand, embraced ‘cinematism' heartily, since, unlike their Parisian Cubist colleagues, they were specifically interested in movement and dynamic phenomena (e.g. Boccioni).

zh: 杜尚相当晚才成为立体主义者，正当“经典”立体主义抱负开始瓦解之际，而且由于天性阴郁，他加入该运动是为了满足他日益强烈的嘲讽冲动，而非因为他是真信徒。（杜尚的厌世有个人原因，已被其传记作者大量发掘。）对他幸运的是，他的一件“讽刺性”立体主义作品，即1912年著名的《下楼梯的裸女》，在美国确立了他作为领先前卫艺术家的名声，他随后在那里获得终身赞助，尽管这他也因这幅画被“官方”立体主义者视为偏离正统、倾向“未来主义”，遭到排斥。《裸女》明显用了类似电影的手法，事实上直接基于E. 马雷等人拍摄的连续动作照片。杜尚有意喜剧性的画旨在展示这样一个事实：虽然“写实主义”仍是终极目标，“第四维”最终只能是物理时间，而“写实”形象（即立体主义写实形象）总是归结为对象的切碎局部形象被相互粘贴或撒在画布上，如那幅臭名昭著的《裸女》。
en: Duchamp became a Cubist rather late in the day, just as ‘classical' Cubist aspirations were beginning to unravel, and, being of a saturnine disposition, he joined the movement in order to indulge his increasing predilection for mockery, rather than because he was a true believer. (There were personal reasons for Duchamp's misanthropy, which have been extensively disinterred by his biographers.) Luckily for him, one of his ‘satirical' Cubist works, the famous Nude Descending a Staircase of 1912, established his name as a leading avant-garde artist in the United States, where he subsequently secured lifelong patronage, though it resulted in his expulsion from the ‘official' Cubist movement (for ‘Futurist' deviationism). The Nude transparently employed ‘cinematic' methods and was, in fact, based directly on stop-motion photographs by E. Marey and others. Duchamp's intentionally comic picture was designed to demonstrate the fact that while ‘realism' remained the ultimate objective, the ‘fourth dimension' could only, in the end, be physical time, and ‘realistic' images (Cubist realist images, that is to say) would always reduce to chopped-up partial images of the object pasted onto one another or strewn over the canvas, as in the notorious Nude.

zh: 杜尚更有雄心；他仍想再现那无法再现的“存在”之流（借用海德格尔的说法），但又不简单地把经验的多样性与丰满归结为一系列局部快照。因此他从1913年起着手于一件能够真正勾画第四维的作品的漫长准备性习作系列。因为杜尚从1913年起的几乎全部作品都是一个单一、连贯计划的一部分，该计划在1925年《大玻璃》（半）完成后又延伸直至其生涯结束，他的全集从我们的观点看特别有趣。字面上说，杜尚的全集由一个单一分布式对象构成，因为杜尚每一件作品都是对他其他作品的准备或发展，且所有作品都可经由直接或间接路径追溯到所有其他作品。这是有意且明确的，因为杜尚的基本目标是创造一个四维实体，而像他这样的全集也许是我们所能拥有的最接近这样一个实体的东西。
en: Duchamp was more ambitious; he still wanted to represent the unrepresentable flux of ‘being' (to employ the Heideggerian term) but without simply reducing the multiplicity and fullness of experience to a series of partial snapshots. He consequently embarked, from 1913, on a long series of preparatory studies of a work which could, truly, adumbrate the fourth dimension. Because almost all of Duchamp's work, from 1913, is part of a single, coherent project, which subsequently, after the (semi-)completion of the Large Glass in 1925, extended itself until the close of his career, his œuvre is particularly interesting from our point of view. It is literally the case that Duchamp's oeuvre consists of a single distributed object, in that each of Duchamp's separate works is a preparation for, or a development of, other works of his, and all may be traced, by direct or circuitous pathways, to all the others. This was intentional and explicit, since Duchamp's basic objective was to create a fourth-dimensional entity, and an œuvre such as his is perhaps as close as we will ever get to possessing such an entity.

zh: 篇幅的考虑——以及我读者的耐心——迫使我把杜尚全集作为时间对象的特征演示集中到一件作品上。确切地说，是借由其中一件作品来看全集。我选择的作品是《大玻璃》众多习作之一（见
）。事实上，它是“毛细管”的习作，这些毛细管从《大玻璃》下半左侧的“制服与号衣墓地”抽出“爱情汽油”，并将其送入中央的锥形“筛子”。这些管子不过是《大玻璃》本身的一个次要细节，然而杜尚却为它们画了一件重要的习作，事实上不止一件。
en: Considerations of space-and the patience of my readers-oblige me to confine the demonstration of the characteristics of Duchamp’s œuvre as a temporal object to a discussion of just one work, or rather, the œuvre ‘seen from’ just one work. The work I have chosen is one of the numerous studies for the Large Glass (see

). In fact, it is a study for the ‘Capillary Tubes' which draw off ‘Love Gasoline' from the ‘Cemetery of Uniforms and Liveries' on the left-hand side of the lower half of the Large Glass and feed it into the conical ‘Sieves' in the centre. These tubes are no more than a minor detail of the Large Glass itself, yet Duchamp devotes an important study to them, indeed, more than one.

zh: 我将讨论的作品被称为《停顿之网》（施瓦茨完整目录第214号；

）。它既是一件独立作品，又是《大玻璃》的准备性习作。乍看之下，它颇像某铁路系统的地图，主枢纽站（在右下，即东南）服务若干向西扇形展开、又向北分支的支线。人们看到线上带编号的小符号（可能是车站）以及其他可能是桥梁或隧道的符号。每条“支线”似乎都终结于某种“终点站”。如果从右下侧看这个“运输系统”，人们能察觉它与《大玻璃》中毛细管的关系，因为在这里该系统从这个角度作了透视投影，而不再采用地图投影。在《大玻璃》中，《网络》所示的二维地图已变成毛细管的三维透视图（通过提供一个从二维世界到三维世界过渡的实例，暗示从三维到四维世界的过渡）。
en: The work I shall discuss is known as The Network of Stoppages (no. 214 in Schwarz's complete catalogue;

). It is both an independent work and a preparatory study for the Large Glass. At first glance, it looks rather like a map of some railway-system, the main depot (at the lower right, or south-east) serving a number of branch-lines fanning out to the west and branching again to the north. One sees little numbered symbols on the lines (which may be stations) and other symbols which might, possibly, be bridges or tunnels. Each ‘branch' seems to come to an end in a ‘terminus' of some kind. If one looks at this ‘transport system' sideways on, from the lower right, one can perceive its relation to the Capillary Tubes in the Large Glass, for here the system is reproduced in ‘perspective' projection (from this point of view), rather than ‘map' projection. In the Large Glass the two-dimensional map shown in the Network has become a three-dimensional perspective view of the Capillary Tubes (hinting at the transition from a 3-d to a 4-d world by providing an instance of the transition from a 2-d world to a 3-d one).

zh: 因此《停顿之网》是对《大玻璃》（部分）的前摄，尽管《网络》在那里只以变换的透视出现。同时《网络》是某些较早作品的滞留。特别是它直接再现了一件叫《三个标准停顿》的作品，它由三块弯曲木模板构成，用来画《网络》中所示的弯曲“轨道”。
en: The Network of Stoppages is therefore a protention towards (part of) the Large Glass, even though the Network only appears there in transformed perspective. At the same time the Network is a retention of certain earlier works. In particular it recapitulates directly a piece called The Three Standard Stoppages which consists of three curved wooden templates which were used to draw the curved ‘tracks' shown in the Network.

zh: 杜尚正在研究的一个观念是，在“第四维”中，对我们显得像“纯粹偶然”的事件将对应于必然。一个“任意”长度或一条“随机”曲线，在第四维中将是真正基本的东西，如“一米”或“一条完全直的线”。相应地，杜尚取三段一米长的线，让它们自由落到涂漆的粘板上，沿这些偶然形成的曲线裁出模板，称为《三个标准停顿》，它们将是“四维”使用的基本几何形式与测量单位。《网络》显然是这些模板的“强滞留”，正如它是朝向毛细管的“强前摄”。
en: One idea Duchamp was working on was that in the ‘fourth dimension' events which seem to us like ‘pure chance' would correspond to necessity. An ‘arbitrary' length, or a ‘random' curve would, in the fourth dimension, be something really basic like ‘one metre' or ‘a perfectly straight line'. Accordingly, Duchamp took three one-metre lengths of string, allowed these to drop freely onto sticky varnished boards, and from these arbitrary curves he cut templates, called the Three Standard Stoppages, which would be the basic geometrical forms and units of measurement for ‘fourth dimensional' use. The network is obviously a ‘strong retention' of these templates, just as it is a ‘strong protention' towards the Capillary Tubes.

zh: 但其中还有更多。如果我们更仔细审视《网络》，会观察到它画在别的东西之上。杜尚未用一块全新的画布，而是在一块上面已有不止一幅画的旧画布上为毛细管做设计工作。事实上，这块画布已被用于显然不同的目的两次。从“顶”层往下数，《停顿之网》由以下构成：
en: But there is much more to it than this. If we inspect the Network more carefully, we observe that it is painted over something else. Duchamp has not used a fresh, pristine canvas, but has done his design-work for the Capillary Tubes on a reused canvas on which more than one image has already been inscribed. In fact, the canvas has already been used twice, for apparently different purposes. Counting from the ‘top' layer downwards, the Network of Stoppages consists of:
1. The ‘map’ of the Network;
zh: 1. 《停顿之网》的“地图”；
2. 一幅（相当淡的）《大玻璃》整体布局的初步线描草图，按杜尚1913年的构思，在许多细节尚未敲定之前；
en: 2. A (quite faint) preliminary line-sketch for the entire layout of the Large Glass, as Duchamp conceived it in 1913, before many details had been worked out;

zh: 3. 一个《春天里的青年与少女》的版本——杜尚1911年的“象征主义”画布，他的第一件重要绘画，以“入门”及可能的乱伦渴望为主题（对他妹妹苏珊娜，他把它作为结婚礼物送给她）；参见
en: 3. A version of Young Man and Girl in Spring- Duchamp's ‘Symbolist' canvas of 1911, his first major painting, dealing with the theme of ‘initiation’ and (possibly) incestuous longing (for his sister, Suzanne, to whom he gave it as a wedding present); cf.

zh: 现在显然，如果杜尚所需要的只是某种可画之物来做设计工作，他完全用得起一块新画布（或干脆一张大纸）用于1与2；尤其如果他打算在草图完成使命后把它们卖给赞助人，如大多数艺术家所做、他自己随后也做的那样。相反，他只用一块画布就生产了相当于一个系列的作品；人们会认为这样的节省反而让自己吃亏——他后来通过生产、或让别人为他生产许多其早期作品的相同摹本来弥补。
en: Now obviously, Duchamp could perfectly well have afforded to use a fresh canvas (or simply a large sheet of paper) for both 1 and 2, if all he required was something drawable-upon to do his design-work; especially if he intended to sell his sketches to patrons once they had served their purpose, as most artists do and as he himself subsequently did. Instead, he produced what amounts to a series of works while using only one canvas; self-defeating parsimony one would have thought-which he made up for later by producing, or having others produce for him, many identical replicas of his earlier works.

zh: 显然，其中必有超出单纯节约的东西。通过创造一幅叠画了三件作品的画布来充当第四件（乃至更多）作品的准备性习作，杜尚正以另一种方式接近第四维——而且从人类学视角看是一种非常清晰的方式。只需再回想这件作品的标题：《停顿之网》。对我们人类学家来说，这些词会让人想起似曾相识的话，因为我们记忆中铭刻着涂尔干的《宗教生活的基本形式》。如果没有，那么至少我们都读过列维-斯特劳斯的《图腾制》（1964），其中引用了涂尔干的话。原始来源是一位达科他印第安人，讨论形而上学：
en: Clearly, there must be more to this than mere economy. By creating a palimpsest of three works to serve as a preparatory study for a fourth (and indeed many more) Duchamp is approaching the fourth dimension in yet another way-and a very perspicuous way from an anthropological perspective. Just recall the title of this work again: The Network of Stoppages. For us anthropologists, those words ring certain bells, because we have Durkheim's Elementary Forms of the Religious Life, engraved on our memories. And if not, then at least we have all read Levi-Strauss's Totemism (1964) where Durkheim's words are quoted. The original source is a Dakota Indian, discussing metaphysics:

zh: [图 9.5/3] 《春天里的青年与少女》，马塞尔·杜尚作（1911）
en: FIG. 9.5/3. The Young Man and Girl in Spring by Marcel Duchamp (1911)

zh: 万物在其运动中，时不时会在某处停下来。鸟在飞翔时停在一处筑巢，停在另一处歇息。人出行时，随其意愿而停。神也是如此停驻。如此明亮美丽的太阳，是他停驻的一处。月亮、星辰、风，他都曾与之同在。树木、动物，都是他停驻之处，印第安人想到这些地方，把祈祷送往那里，以到达神停驻之处，求得帮助与祝福。（涂尔干，引自列维-斯特劳斯《图腾制》: 98）
en: Everything as it moves, now and then, here and there, makes stops. The bird as it flies stops in one place to make its nest, and in another to rest in its flight. A man when he goes forth stops when he wills. So the god has stopped. The sun, which is so bright and beautiful, is one place where he has stopped. The moon, the stars, the winds, he has been with. The trees, the animals, are all where he has stopped, and the Indian thinks of these places and sends his prayers there to reach the place where the god has stopped and win help and a blessing. (Durkheim, quoted in Levi-Strauss, Totemism: 98)

zh: 列维-斯特劳斯在讨论柏格森的过程中引用这段话，他说柏格森在《创造进化论》中提出了惊人相似的观点，而且柏格森无疑熟悉涂尔干书中引用的这段话。列维-斯特劳斯接着评论：
en: Levi-Strauss quotes this passage in the course of a discussion of Bergson, who, he says, propounded remarkably similar views in Creative Evolution, and who was undoubtedly familiar with the passage in Durkheim in which they are quoted. Levi-Strauss goes on to remark:

zh: 为凸显两者的相似之处，下面整段引自《两个来源》［《道德与宗教的两个来源》］中柏格森总结其形而上学的那一段：
en: The better to underline the comparison, let us quote without break from the paragraph in Les Deux Sources [The Two Sources of Morality and Religion] where Bergson sums up his metaphysics:

zh: 一股巨大的创造力量奔涌而出，穿过物质，从它那里尽可能多地取得自己所需的东西。它在大多数地方停了下来；这些停顿在我们眼中转化为众多活物种的外观，即有机体的外观，在其中我们的知觉（本质上是分析性与综合性的）区分出众多元素组合以履行众多功能；但组织化过程只是停顿本身，一个类似于脚印的简单行动，一脚落下，成千上万的沙粒随即排成一个图案。
en: A great current of creative energy gushes forth through matter, to obtain from it what it can. At most points it is stopped; these stops are transmuted, in our eyes, into the appearances of so many living species, i.e., of organisms in which our perception, being essentially analytical and synthetic, distinguishes a multitude of elements combining to fulfil a multitude of functions; but the process of organisation was only the stop itself, a simple act analogous to the impress of a foot which instantaneously causes thousands of grains of sand to contrive to form a pattern.

zh: 两种描述如此精确地一致，以至于读完它们后，声称柏格森能够理解图腾制度背后的东西，因为他自己的思想（在他不知情时）与图腾民族的思想相契合，似乎不那么冒险了。那么它们共同的是什么？似乎这种关系源于同一个愿望：以总体方式把握哲学家称为连续与不连续的实在的两个方面；源于同样拒绝在两者之间选择；源于同样努力把它们看作通向同一真理的互补视角。（列维-斯特劳斯1964: 98；参考文献见原书）
en: The two accounts agree so exactly that it may seem less risky, after reading them, to claim that Bergson was able to understand what lay behind totemism because his own thought, unbeknownst to him, was in sympathy with that of totemic peoples. What is it, then, that they have in common? It seems that the relationship results from one and the same desire to apprehend in a total fashion the two aspects of reality which the philosopher terms continuous and discontinuous; from the same refusal to choose between the two; and from the same effort to see them as complementary perspectives giving on to the same truth. (Levi-Strauss 1964: 98; for refs. see original)

zh: 现在，不难把握杜尚《停顿之网》的主题与其呈现的特殊方式——像千层蛋糕那样，把一件件作品叠在一起——之间的联系。“网—络”既向我们展示一个停顿之网，也是一个停顿之网，即一连串“停栖之处”，在其中杜尚在其“飞行”中以他的能动性索引、一件特定艺术作品的形式变得可见。《网络》看起来像“地图”，因为它是一张时间“地图”的一部分。但这只能是一张四维地图。像柏格森一样，杜尚不看重单凭眼睛所见的外观，也不看重以错觉再现外观的手法。像柏格森一样，他不信任我们“仅仅分析性与综合性”的知觉，转而寻求“穿过物质涌出”的“创造能量之流”（即绵延，或海德格尔式“存在”）。这就是第四维。
en: It is surely not difficult to grasp the connection, now, between the subject-matter of Duchamp's Network of Stoppages, and the peculiar manner in which it has been presented, as a layer-cake of artworks placed one over the other. The ‘Net-work', both shows us a Network of Stoppages, and also is a network of stoppages, i.e. a series of ‘perchings' at which Duchamp, in his ‘flight' becomes visible in the form of an index of his agency, a particular work of art. The Network looks like a ‘map' because it is part of a ‘map' of time. But this can only be a four-dimensional map. Like Bergson, Duchamp downplays the ‘merely' visible, or its illusionistic representation. Like Bergson, he distrusts our perception ‘which is merely analytic and synthetic', and seeks instead the ‘current of creative energy' (i.e. durée, or Heideggerian ‘being') which ‘gushes forth through matter'. This is the fourth dimension.

zh: 用胡塞尔式术语说，《停顿之网》的透明分层与由滞留、滞留的滞留等等构成的绵延概念之间，有一处惊人的相似。《网络》是对《大玻璃》的前摄，就滞留而言，首先保留的是《大玻璃》尚未敲定内容时的初步布局。透过这一滞留，又保留着杜尚象征主义的开端，即对超越与从乱伦渴望（“入门”）中解脱的渴求，那使他走上随后遵循的道路。杜尚让我们看到他“下沉”的过去作为其现在的一个可变换成分，作为在其间生命过程中已被超越之物而被滞留。的确，有充分的艺术史理由把《大玻璃》解释为《春天里的青年与少女》的一个变换版本、一段遥远记忆（见如Golding 1973: 第3章）。
en: In Husserlian terms, there is a most startling analogy between the transparent layering of The Network of Stoppages, and the concept of durée constituted out of retentions, retentions of retentions, and so on. The Network is a protention towards the Large Glass, which is a retention, first, of the original abstract layout for that work (before its content was finalized) and secondly a retention, from this retention, of Duchamp's Symbolist beginnings, the thirst for transcendence and release from incestuous longing (‘initiation') which set him on the path he subsequently followed. Duchamp allows us to see his ‘sinking' past as a transformable component of his present, retained as something already superseded in the course of his intervening life. And indeed, there are ample art-historical reasons for interpreting The Large Glass as a transformed version, a distant memory, of The Young Man and Girl in Spring (see e.g. Golding 1973: ch. 3).

zh: 因此我所提议的可以称为艺术家全集的“达科他”模型；每件艺术作品，正如杜尚的画如此惊人地向我们揭示的，是能动性“停驻”并采取可见形式的地方。《大玻璃》本身被杜尚加了一个副标题“玻璃中的延迟”（retard en verre），恰恰暗示这一观念（玻璃像照相底片一样让第四维投来的影子暂时停驻，并捕获其可见痕迹）。在后来作品中这一程序被更明确地重复：例如在《Tu m'》（1918）中，它以错视画“影子”呈现杜尚先前“现成品”作品（《自行车轮》（1913）、《帽架》（1914）等）。
en: What I am proposing, therefore, may be called a ‘Dakota' model of the artist's oeuvre; each artwork, as Duchamp's picture so strikingly reveals to us, is a place where agency ‘stops' and assumes visible form. The Large Glass itself was subtitled, by its creator, as a ‘delay in glass' (retard en verre), suggesting precisely this idea (the glass, like a photographic plate) delays the passage of the shadows of the fourth dimension, and captures their visible traces. In later works the procedure is repeated more explicitly: for instance, in Tu m’ (1918), which features trompe-l’œil ‘shadows' of Duchamp's previous ‘ready-made' works (the Bicycle-Wheel (1913), the Hat-rack (1914), etc.).

zh: 换言之，每件杜尚作品都邀请我们对所有杜尚作品采取一个特定视角，经常通过提供对过去与未来作品的明确引用或指涉，但也以更省略的方式勾画滞留与前摄。把每一处时间的“停栖点”当作视点，依次看过去，便能看到前摄与滞留构成的内部指涉网络怎样把全集联结起来，又怎样变换。这个无限可变的网络的总和，就是不可表象但非常可概念化、绝非“神秘”的第四维。以这种方式杜尚把自己变成一位诙谐而世俗的灵魂引路人。
en: Each Duchamp work, in other words, invites us to adopt a particular perspective on all Duchamp's works, often by providing explicit quotations or references to past and future works, though also adumbrating retentions and protentions in a more elliptical fashion. The sum total of the infinitely transformable network of internal references (protentions and retentions) uniting the œuvre from all of these temporal ‘perches'-which we can only, in fact, adopt serially, is the unrepresentable but very conceptualizable and by no means ‘mystic' fourth dimension. In this way Duchamp triumphantly vindicates himself as a comic, secularist, psychopomp.

zh: 此时，对杜尚全集的讨论才触及表面，但这里得打住了，尽管我希望我已说得足够多，以鼓励任何感兴趣的读者进一步深入这一主题，因为可得文献与记录异常丰富且有启发。我的目的只是确立这一点：杜尚的主体性、他的内在绵延，作为一系列环节、或“延迟”或“停栖之处”，具体见于他的能动性留下的客观痕迹，即他的艺术作品与他为伴随它们而生产的文本。在这里，我们以公开、可接近的形式，拥有胡塞尔为阐明纯粹主观的认知或意识过程而描述的“前摄与滞留变样的连续统的连续统”。换言之，作为一个分布式对象，杜尚的意识、他作为施动者的存在之流本身，不仅“对我们可接近”，而且已采取了这种形式。杜尚已简单地变成这个对象，如今以无数形式、作为这些分离的人格部件、或偶像、或皮、或被珍视的贵重物，在世界上流转作响。于是我们回到起点。但还有一步要走。杜尚是（或曾是）一个个体心智，一个行使一种特定能动性的特定人。那么不是由个体在一生中、而是由集体在更长时间中生产的艺术呢；换言之，关于集体“传统”我们能说什么？能否扩展我们刚才构建的“艺术家全集”模型，以涵盖更宽的东西、某种对应于“文化传统”的东西，以便我们也能把它看作一个在结构上与作为时间过程或绵延的意识同构的分布式对象？
en: At this point, without having done more than scratch the surface, I curtail further discussion of Duchamp's oeuvre, though I hope that I have said enough to encourage any interested readers to pursue the subject further, since the literature and documentation available is unusually extensive and revealing. My purpose is only to establish the point that Duchamp's subjectivity, his inner durée is concretely instantiated, as a series of moments, or ‘delays' or ‘perchings', in the objective traces of his agency, that is, his artworks and the texts he produced to go with them. Here we have, in public, accessible, form, the 'continuum of continua of protentional and retentional modifications' described by Husserl for the purposes of elucidating the purely subjective process of cognition, or consciousness. In other words, as a distributed object, Duchamp's consciousness, the very flux of his being as an agent, is not just ‘accessible to us' but has assumed this form. Duchamp has simply turned into this object, and now rattles around the world, in innumerable forms, as these detached person-parts, or idols, or skins, or cherished valuables. So we return to our starting-point. But there is one more step to be taken. Duchamp is (or was) an individual mind, one particular person exercising one particular agency. What about the art produced, not by individuals over a lifetime, but by collectivities over longer periods of time; what, in other words, can we say about collective ‘traditions'. Can we, so to speak, expand the model that we have just constructed of ‘the artist's oeuvre' to encompass something wider, something corresponding to a ‘cultural tradition' so that we can see that, too, as a distributed object structurally isomorphous to consciousness as a temporal process, or durée?

zh: 这是我在结束本作时将转向的最后一个问题。
en: This is the final problem to which I will turn, in concluding the present work.

zh: 9.6　毛利会堂
en: 9.6　The Maori Meeting House

zh: 与刚提出的问题相关的大量资料最近由罗杰·奈奇（1996）提供。他完成了一项详细研究，涵盖北岛毛利人在约1850与1930年间建造的所有现存或有照片记录的会堂，这些会堂又是较早十九世纪与欧洲人到来之前酋长房屋（以宏伟壮丽为念而竖立的大型建筑）的发展（

，来自Neich, fig. 68）。当代毛利“会堂”在19世纪后半叶逐渐成形，尤其是在1870年以后，那一时期毛利人发现自己无法再经由传统战争手段彼此（或与欧洲人）竞争。他们的竞争精神越来越集中于建造大型、精心雕刻与彩绘的会堂，每个毛利社区都尽其所能在这方面压倒邻人与对手。因此毛利会堂的总体构成一个特定艺术生产类型，跨越毛利历史中一个特定历史阶段（在许多方面是一个光荣时期，当代毛利人正当地以自豪回忆），它可以在我们所需的意义上被视为“连贯”。也就是说，所有毛利会堂都遵循一个共同“平面图”，都为一个共同目的而设计，即把建造者共同体的财富、文化修养、技艺和祖先遗产化为看得见的建筑，并作为确保非本社区、可能在那里受招待的人充满嫉妒并被彻底震慑的手段。正如尼克·托马斯就毛利艺术所写：
en: Copious data relevant to the question just raised have recently been provided by Roger Neich (1996). He has completed a detailed study of all the extant or photographically documented meeting houses constructed by the Maori of North Island between c.1850 and 1930, which were, in turn, a development of chiefly houses (large structures erected with magnificence in mind) of the earlier nineteenth century and the pre-European period (

from Neich, fig. 68). The present-day Maori ‘meeting house' came into its own during the latter half of the nineteenth century, especially from 1870 onwards, a period during which the Maori found themselves unable to compete with one another (or Europeans) via the traditional warlike means. Their competitive spirit focused more and more on the construction of large, elaborately carved and painted meeting houses, each Maori community trying, so far as lay within its power, to outdo its neighbours and rivals in this respect. The totality of Maori meeting houses, therefore, constitutes a particular genre of art production, over a particular historical phase in the course of Maori history (in many ways, a glorious period, which contemporary Maoris rightly recall with pride), which can be considered ‘coherent' in the sense we require. All Maori meeting houses, that is to say, followed a common ‘ground plan', all were designed with a common purpose, namely, to serve as an objectification of the wealth, sophistication, technical skill, and ancestral endowment of the community responsible for the construction, and as a means to ensure that persons not of this community, who might be entertained there, would be consumed with jealousy and thoroughly intimidated. As Nick Thomas has written, apropos of Maori art:

zh: 房屋……不是“象征”……而是一个集体力量的载体。它们同时索引一个群体自身的活力，并使外人觉得自己势弱，甚至削弱他们的实际力量。功能与意义、使用与表达、工具性与象征主义之间的区分，遮蔽了这些部落效力的集体呈现中整合的、过程性的东西……（Thomas 1995: 103）
en: houses ... were not ‘symbols' . . . but vehicles of a collectivity's power. They simultaneously indexed a group's own vitality and ideally or effectively disempowered others. Distinctions between function and meaning, use and expression, instrumentality and symbolism obscure what was integrated and processual in these collective presentations of tribal efficacy ... (Thomas 1995: 103)

zh: 毛利会堂可能是许多各自工作的艺术家与建造者共同留下的成果，他们在不同时间于不同社群工作，各努力生产某种独特之物，但所有都是一个共同历史轨迹、一个共同文化系统、一个共同意识形态与政治目的的表达。因此我们有权像奈奇那样把它们归为一组，因为它们在相关时期构成“毛利性”作为集体经验之物质表达的“最终共同路径”。
en: Maori meeting houses may have been the collective production of many separate artists and builders, working in separate communities at different times, each striving to produce something distinctive, yet all are expressions of a common historical trajectory, a common cultural system, a common ideological and political purpose. We are entitled, therefore, to group them together, as Neich does, since they constituted the ‘final common pathway' for the physical expression of ‘Maoridom' as a collective experience, during the relevant period.

zh: 因为这些集体“能动性索引”是房屋——具有非常特殊、自有特征的人工制品（参见Hugh-Jones and Carsten 1995）——它们拥有使它们特别适合投射集体能动性的特征。首先，房屋在最简单的意义上是“集体”的，即人们在其中聚集、并由它们联结；这适用于任何房屋，也是为什么这么多社会群体被称为“房屋”的原因（Lévi-Strauss；参见Hugh-Jones and Carstens, op. cit.）。其次，房屋是由许多可分离的标准部件构成的复杂人工制品；因此它们是有组织的、或“有机”的实体，不同于比如说一只碗或一支矛，无论制作多么精美。它们的有机规划与拆卸重装、改造重饰的能力，使它们能把历史过程中的有机联系具体呈现出来。最后——而且首要地——它们是身体。房屋是身体的身体。房屋是身体，因为它们是像身体一样有入口与出口的容器。房屋是住着活人的腔体。房屋是身体，因为它们有强壮的骨骼与坚实的外壳，因为它们有艳丽、催眠的皮，既迷惑又恐吓；因为它们有感觉与表达的器官——从窗户与窥孔向外凝视的眼睛，在夜中回荡的声音。进入房屋就是进入一个心智、一种感受力；尤其如果它是毛利人习惯建造的那种房屋。像许多传统心理学家一样，毛利人把心智与意图定位于内脏。进入房屋就是进入祖先的肚腹，感到自己彻底被无所不在的祖先包围；头顶是祖先的肋骨，以精美装饰的椽子形式向祖先脊柱——脊檩，祖先连续性的源头——汇聚。四面，祖先的偶像俯视着来人，目光令人着迷，把观看者困入它们的思维过程（参见上文第7章论偶像）。祖先的飞散拟像数不胜数，以惊人的速度在屋内穿梭；所有仅仅私人、独立的思考都被压倒，只有那些实际从房屋发出的认知、那些作为房屋结构本身一部分的认知，才是可得的。
en: Because these collective ‘indexes of agency' were houses-artefacts with very special characteristics all their own (cf. Hugh-Jones and Carsten 1995)—they possess features which render them especially suited to the projection of collective agency. First of all, houses are ‘collective' in the simplest sense of all, that people collect in them, and are joined together by them; this applies to any house and is the reason why so many social groups are referred to as ‘houses’ (Lévi-Strauss; cf. Hugh-Jones and Carstens, op. cit.). Secondly, houses are complex artefacts consisting of many separate, standard, parts; they are thus organized, or ‘organic' entities, unlike, say, a bowl or a spear, however wonderfully wrought. Their organic plan and capacity for disassembly and reassembly, remodelling and redecoration allows them to objectify the organic connectedness of historical processes. And finally-and above all--they are bodies. The house is a body for the body. Houses are bodies because they are containers which, like the body, have entrances and exits. Houses are cavities filled with living contents. Houses are bodies because they have strong bones and armoured shells, because they have gaudy, mesmerizing skins which beguile and terrify; and because they have organs of sense and expression—eyes which peer out through windows and spyholes, voices which reverberate through the night. To enter a house is to enter a mind, a sensibility; especially if it is such a house as the Maori were accustomed to make. Like many traditional psychologists, the Maori located mind and intention in the viscera. To enter a house is to enter the belly of the ancestor and to be overwhelmed by the encompassing ancestral presence; overhead are the ribs of the ancestor, in the form of the superbly decorated rafters which converge towards the ancestral backbone, the ridge-pole-the fountainhead of ancestral continuity. On all sides, idols of ancestral beings gaze down hypnotically, entrapping the onlooker in their thought-processes (cf. above, Ch. 7 on idols). The flying simulacra of the ancestors criss-cross this interior space with unbelievable rapidity and profusion; all merely private, independent, thought is overwhelmed and only those cognitions which actually emanate from the house, those cognitions which are part of the house's very structure, are attainable.

zh: 奈奇全面讨论了毛利会堂的宇宙论“象征意义”。他详尽说明了每座会堂怎样被明确视为一位社群祖先的身体，并以这位祖先的名字命名。祖先借这种形态重新在场。会堂是祖先此时此地拥有的身体，使他能在当下行使能动性，远不只是曾在别处生活和行动留下的痕迹。把它称为“象征”显得不妥。同时房屋是多个相连的身体，一个瓦格纳意义上（1991；参见7.11节）的身体“分形”，因为它由祖先后裔的身体构成，按谱系继承，无论生者死者。脊檩客观化酋长世系的谱系连续性（按观念中的长子继承顺序），而下行的椽子指示两侧旁支的增殖。它们以称为科怀怀（kowhaiwhai）的夺目纹样装饰（
，来自Neich, fig. 17），唤起永远多产、永远增殖的库马拉（甘薯，为毛利人提供主食的植物）的卷须与走茎。身体、谱系、园圃，在这里同时显现，共同发挥作用。聚集在屋中的社区活成员，可以说只是“陈设”。他们是其坚固、持久结构的移动附属物，最终将作为“固定装置”被吸收进其中。
en: Neich provides a very comprehensive discussion of the cosmological ‘symbolism' of Maori meeting houses. He shows in great detail how each such house was explicitly conceptualized as the body of the eponymous ancestor of the community, who was not so much ‘memorialized' in the house which bore his name, as reinstated in this form. The house was not a surviving trace of the ancestor's existence and agency at some other, distant, coordinates, but was the body which he possessed in the here and now, and through which his agency was exercised in the immediate present (to describe this as ‘symbolic' is obviously a misnomer). At the same time the house was a multiplicity of connected bodies, a bodily ‘fractal' in Wagner's sense (1991; cf. Sect. 7.11), since it consisted of the bodies of the ancestor's descendants, by genealogical succession, both living and deceased. The ridge-pole objectifies the genealogical continuity of the chiefly line (notionally by male primogeniture) while the descending rafters indicate the proliferation of cadet lines on either side. These were decorated with captivating patterns of the type called kowhaiwhai (

from Neich, fig. 17), which evoked the tendrils and runners of the ever-productive, ever proliferating kumara, the sweet potato plant which provided the Maori with their staple diet. Body, genealogy, gardens, were all copresent and synergically active. The living members of the community, gathered in the house, were, so to speak, only ‘furnishings'. They were mobile appurtenances of its solid, enduring structure, into which they would eventually be absorbed as ‘fixtures'.

zh: 但本节的要点不是讨论毛利会堂的文化意义，鉴于奈奇及其同事已就此主题发表的优秀著作，那将是冗余。前面的评论只是重申本作较早部分论证的论点：像毛利会堂这样的人工制品不是“象征”而是能动性索引。在此例中，能动性属于集体，也属于祖先，主要在政治上发挥作用。
en: But the point of this section is not to discuss the cultural significance of the Maori meeting house, which would be redundant given the excellent work that has already been published on this subject by Neich and his colleagues. The preceding remarks only reiterate the thesis, argued in earlier parts of this work, that artefacts like Maori meeting houses are not ‘symbols' but indexes of agency. In this instance, the agency is collective, ancestral, and essentially political in tone.

zh: 我引入这些材料的目的是探索“传统”主题。我们能在多大程度上把分布于时空的毛利会堂全部范围，作为一个单一、连贯、分布于时空的对象来研究，它在某种意义上于历史与集体尺度上重演认知或意识的过程？幸而通过奈奇所作的极其细致的研究，我们确实能朝这个方向进展。为展示这一点，我只需复制一张奈奇本人设计、出现在其书第220页的表（

）。奈奇的表《若干具象绘画传统的传递》采用如下布局。表的左—右轴对应历史时间轴（1870与1930之间），而上—下轴（未标注）隐含地对应地理空间；即位于水平轴上的会堂（带数字与字母的大黑点）在空间上是或曾是相邻的。数字指奈奇全面目录中的特定会堂，字母对应毛利具象绘画的“传统”，它们从1870年起开始发展与增殖——在此之前只有毛利雕刻是“具象”的，而（会堂上的）绘画采用科怀怀及其衍生风格。我们实际上不需要深入讨论奈奇的材料，因为它非常详细且语境化。我主要想做的只是强调并探索一个读者必然已经想到的观察：奈奇的图与我作为
呈现的图——我试图提供“艺术家全集”抽象模型的点—箭头图——之间有大量相似。
en: My aim in introducing this material is to explore the theme of ‘traditions'. To what extent can we study the whole gamut of Maori meeting houses, distributed in space and time, as a single, coherent, object, distributed in space and time, which, in a certain sense, recapitulates, on the historical and collective scale, the processes of cognition or consciousness? Fortunately, through the very meticulous studies undertaken by Neich, we can indeed make progress in this direction. In order to show this, I need do little more than reproduce a table, devised by Neich himself, which appears on page 220 of his book (

). Neich's table ‘"The Transmission of Selected Figurative Painting Traditions' is organized in the following way. The left-to-right axis of the table corresponds to the axis of historical time (between 1870 and 1930) while the top-to-bottom axis, which is unlabelled, corresponds, implicitly, to geographical space; that is, meeting houses (the large black spots with numbers and letters in them) which lie on a horizontal axis are or were spatially contiguous. The numbers denote particular meeting houses in Neich's comprehensive catalogue of the same, and the letters correspond to ‘traditions' of Maori figurative painting, which began to develop and proliferate from 1870 onwards-before which time only Maori carving was ‘figurative' and painting (on meeting houses) was in the kowhaiwhai style and developments therefrom. We do not actually need to discuss Neich's material in any depth, since it is very detailed and contextual. All that I primarily wish to do is to underline and explore an observation that must have inevitably occurred to the reader already, that there is a great deal of similarity between Neich's diagram and the diagram I presented as
-the spot-and-arrow diagram in which I sought to provide an abstract model of the ‘artist’s œuvre'.

zh: 奈奇不用箭头，而用简单线条连接其历史—地理网络中的节点；他不是在以前摄与滞留来思考，后者从任何给定“现在”时刻、或从任何给定艺术作品完成时刻的时间立场，总是有确定方向性，朝向过去（记忆、重演）或朝向未来（计划、初步草图）。同时，奈奇像大多数艺术史家一样以“进步”来思考；从过去朝向未来，因为他整本书的前提（并非不公正地）是独特毛利艺术“发展”的观念。所以我猜如果他在表上用箭头而非线条，他的箭头都会是右指的。但这并不真正合乎逻辑，因为“传统传递”概念真正首要涉及的是：在“T₀”时刻受委托装饰房屋的艺术家“记得”他在“T₋₁”于别处某先前建筑上目睹的范本。“传统”的传递、模型的重演，是记忆的客观化，因此内在地是回顾的。所以箭头最合逻辑地应不是从左到右，而是从右到左。但这也不行，因为无论建造毛利会堂的艺术家心里想什么，那肯定不是规规矩矩地照搬其他社区在不久或更远的过去某时建造的房屋。如前强调，这些房屋的全部要点是摧毁对手社区成员的（建筑）自尊，通过以更高的宏伟与精湛客观化建房社区的祖先，使其凌驾于所有他人祖先之上（这意味着除其他外，把对帕克哈“白人”艺术的指涉纳入装饰，与“传统”艺术形式并列）。不只是毛利会堂纳入“创新”（即非传统要素，后来被模仿而自身成为“传统”），每座房屋都完全是一个“创新”（参见Wagner 1977），因为房屋朝向未来，即投入其建造的努力的预期结果——政治胜利。建房是一个集体、意向的行动，而“行动”内在地朝向未来。由会堂索引的“祖先能动性”同样朝向未来；祖先的身体/房屋不是尸体或对逝者的纪念。所以再一次，似乎我们应让箭头从左到右、朝向未来。经过这一切，似乎奈奇完全不用箭头是做得对的，因为那样做会产生悖论；作为“传统”人工制品，毛利会堂不可否认是回顾的，作为政治姿态它们是前瞻的。然而会堂怎么能同时既前瞻又回顾？
en: Instead of arrows, Neich joins the nodal points in his historico-geographical network by simple lines; he is not thinking in terms of protentions and retentions which, from any given ‘now' moment, or from the temporal standpoint of any given work of art at the moment of its completion, always have a definite directionality, towards the past (memory, recapitulation) or towards the future (project, preliminary sketch). Meanwhile, Neich is thinking, as most art historians do, in terms of ‘progress'; from the past and towards the future, because his whole book is premised, not unjustifiably, on the idea of the ‘development' of a distinctive Maori art. So I guess that had he used arrows instead of lines on his table, his arrows would all have been rightwards-pointing ones. But this is not really logical, in that the concept of ‘the transmission of traditions' really involves, primarily, the artist, commissioned to decorate a house at time ‘T-zero’ ‘remembering' an exemplar that he witnessed, somewhere else, on some previous building, at ‘T-minus-one'. The transmission of a ‘tradition', the recapitulation of a model, is the objectification of memory, and thus inherently retrospective. So the arrows ought, most logically, to point not from left to right, but from right to left. But this will not do either, because whatever the artists who made the Maori meeting houses had in mind, it certainly was not to reproduce, tamely, the houses that had been constructed, by other communities, sometime in the immediate or more distant past. The whole point of these houses, as was emphasized earlier, was to bring about the crushing of the (architectural) self-esteem of members of rival communities, to exalt the ancestors of the house-building community over everybody else's ancestors, by objectifying them with superior magnificence and sophistication (which meant, inter alia, incorporating references to pakeha ‘white'-art into the decor, alongside ‘traditional' art forms). It is not just that Maori meeting houses incorporated ‘innovations' (i.e. non-traditional elements which, later, being imitated, became ‘traditions' in themselves), each house was totally an ‘innovation' (cf. Wagner 1977) in that the house was orientated towards the future, the political triumph which would be the anticipated outcome of the effort invested in its construction. The building of the house was a collective, intentional, action, and ‘action' is intrinsically future-orientated. The ‘agency of the ancestor' of which the house is an index, is equally future-orientated; the ancestor's body/house is not a corpse or a memorial to the departed. So once again, it seems that we should make our arrows point from left to right, towards the future. After all this, it may seem that Neich has done well to refrain from using arrows at all, in that doing so results in paradoxes; as ‘traditional' artefacts, Maori meeting houses are undeniably retrospective, as political gestures they are prospective. Yet how can meeting houses be both prospective and retrospective at the same time?

zh: 但我们已经遇到并（我希望）克服了这个困难。人工制品或事件在任何绝对意义上、或如时间哲学家倾向说的从永恒的视角，从来不是传统或创新的。“传统”人工制品（或事件）只有从后世视角、作为能从中看见前作轮廓的屏幕或透明片来看，才是“传统”的。传统对象被把握为滞留、滞留的滞留，等等。相反，“创新”对象（或事件）只有在我们把自己置于它在时间之前（即它尚未、或正要存在的时刻）的条件下才是创新的——以便我们同样能把它看作更后对象可被前摄于其上的屏幕，作为前摄、前摄的前摄，等等。因此由奈奇图上展示的会堂总体构成的时间对象，不在于一个能在单一概观映射中被总体化的时间关系网络；而只在于一个由对应于不同时间（与空间）立足点的一整系列此类映射构成的“档案”；其中每一个都产生任何给定会堂与时空上相邻的其他会堂之间滞留与前摄关系的独特分布。这种对历史人工制品组合中传统与创新的持续移动视角的逻辑强制性，意味着理解艺术史的过程本质上类似于意识本身的过程，后者同样以持续的视角流变为标志。
en: But we have encountered, and (I hope) surmounted this difficulty already. An artefact or event is never either traditional or innovatory in any absolute sense, or, as time-philosophers are inclined to put it, sub specie aeternitatis. A ‘traditional' artefact (or event) is only ‘traditional' when viewed from a latterday perspective, and as a screen, or transparency, through which its precursors are adumbrated. The traditional object is grasped as a retention, a retention of retentions, and so on. Conversely, an ‘innovatory' object (or event) is innovatory only on condition that we situate ourselves anterior to it in time (i.e. at a moment in time at which it has not yet, or is just about to, come into existence)-so that we can likewise see it as a screen through which still later objects may be protended, as a protention, protention of protentions, etc. The temporal object constituted by the totality of the meeting houses displayed on Neich’s diagram consists therefore, not of a network of temporal relations which can be totalized in a single synoptic mapping; but only as a ‘file' consisting of a whole series of such mappings corresponding to different temporal (and spatial) points of vantage; each one of which generates a distinctive distribution of retentional and protentional relations between any given meeting house and its spatio-temporal neighbours. The logically mandatory nature of such a continuously shifting perspective on tradition and innovation in an historical assemblage of artefacts means that the process of understanding art history is essentially akin to the processes of consciousness itself, which is marked, likewise, by a continuous perspectival flux.

zh: 更具体地说，我们可以把任何给定会堂从后世视角解释为对此前会堂的客观化形式的“记忆”。的确，就毛利建造者的认知过程而言，“记忆”是负责传递传承知识、换言之房屋所体现的“传统”的官能。但这不会是“传统”，除非“凭记忆”建造的房屋的建造者知道自己记得的范本也有更早的范本，而它们反过来又是那些前件的记忆，回溯入过去。每座房屋不仅体现其直接范本的记忆，而且体现一个累积的记忆系列、记忆的记忆，等等。也就是说，它随身携带绵延的全部厚度，不仅属于一个“现在”——其建造日期的时间坐标——而且属于一个回溯入过去、又被重新拉入现在的延展时间场。
en: To express this more concretely, we can interpret any given meeting house, viewed from the latter-day perspective, as a ‘memory' in objectified form, of meeting houses anterior to this one. Indeed, in terms of the cognitive processes of the Maori builders, ‘memory' is the faculty responsible for the transmission of the lore, the ‘tradition' in other words-which the house embodies. But this would not be ‘tradition' unless the memory-antecedents of the house constructed ‘from memory' were remembered as having antecedents of their own, of which they, in turn, were memories, back into the past. Each house embodies not just the memory of its immediate exemplar, but a cumulative series of memories, memories of memories, and so on. That is to say, it carries with it the whole thickness of durée, and belongs not just to a ‘now'-the temporal coordinates of its dates of construction-but to an extended temporal field which reaches back into the past and which is drawn up into the present again.

zh: 相反，每座会堂都是未来房屋的一个计划、一系列尚未建成的会堂的“草图”。我们倾向于把人工制品、尤其像这些相当辉煌的人工制品，看作仿佛体现了其制作者的最终意图。但任何曾与建造任何东西（哪怕郊区住宅的扩建）打过交道的人都会立即认出这几乎不是事实。一旦决定总得建点什么，最后建起来的，就是在诸多实际难处和限制之下所能作出的最好折中。我们可能认为我们的房屋扩建远优于邻人的，但那不意味着我们不想把整个拆掉重来，如果那是可行选项。我们当然有权假设同样的抱负与现实之差进入了毛利会堂的建造过程。回想这些是在公开竞争精神中竖立的，用来向邻近社群表明，本社群连同它的众多祖先都更胜一筹。在此语境中，会堂再大、再精美、再昂贵、再宏伟也不为过。但十九世纪毛利人事实上贫困、受压迫、人数递减，而他们祖先提供的援助最终是有限的。被建造的房屋恐怕远非毛利人想建造的房屋；它们也许优于此前房屋，可以说也许优于对手社区的会堂（尽管这可能不会在公开场合被承认）——但它们几乎不可能优于、甚至达到当初设想的样子。它们只是朝向终极会堂的“草图”或“前摄”，后者出于实际原因将永远不可实现。作为“草图”的会堂体现了在有朝一日盖一座胜过所有会堂的会堂的承诺；而正是这种一旦环境真正有利就建造“终极”会堂的“威胁”，与“已实现”的房屋本身一样，是针对邻人的。
en: Conversely, each meeting house is a project for future houses, a ‘sketch' towards a series of as yet unbuilt houses. We are inclined to see artefacts, especially rather splendid artefacts like these, as if they embodied the final intentions of their makers. But anyone who has ever had anything to do with building anything (even an extension to a suburban home) will instantly recognize that this is hardly the case. What gets built is whatever seems the best possible compromise in the light of all the practical difficulties and constraints entering into the situation; given that the decision to build ‘something or other' has already been taken. We may think that our house-extension is vastly superior to our neighbours', but that does not mean that we would not like to tear the whole thing down and start again, were that a practicable option. We are certainly entitled to suppose that the same disparity between aspiration and actuality entered into the process of building Maori meeting houses. These, it will be recalled, were erected in an overt spirit of competition, in order to indexicalize the superiority of one community, and its legions of ancestors, over other, neighbouring, communities. No meeting house could, in this context, be too large, too sophisticated, too expensive and magnificent. But the nineteenth-century Maori were, as a matter of fact, impoverished, oppressed, and diminishing in numbers, while the assistance afforded them by their ancestors was, in the end, finite. The houses that were built were far, probably, from being the houses the Maori would have liked to build; they were, perhaps, superior to the houses which preceded them, they might, arguably, be superior to the meeting houses of rival communities (though this would probably not be conceded in public)-but they could hardly be superior, or even equal, to what they were intended to be. There were only ‘sketches' or ‘protentions towards' the ultimate meeting house, which, for practical reasons, would always remain unrealizable. The meeting house as a ‘sketch' embodied, the promise, some time in the future, to build the meeting house to beat all meeting houses; and it was this ‘threat' to build, once circumstances became really favourable, the ‘ultimate' meeting house, which was aimed at the neighbours, as much as the ‘realized' house itself.

zh: 于是我们得以把毛利会堂总体看作一个被放大的认知过程、一场内在绵延的运动，既是一个现存对象的集合，也是关于时间已抹去之对象的文献。把所有毛利会堂放在一起看，就能追踪其中的思想怎样运动。一边是记忆回溯过去，另一边是抱负伸向尚未成真、也许永远不会成真的未来。通过对这些人工制品的研究，我们得以把“心智”把握为把心智化为可见事物的一连串公开行动所构成的外在（而永存）的格局，同时把握为一个集体的演进意识，超越个体我思与任何特定此时此地的坐标。
en: Thus we are enabled to see the totality of Maori meeting houses as a cognitive process writ large, a movement of inner durée as well as a collection of existing objects, and documents appertaining to objects which time has obliterated. The Maori meeting house (in its totalized form) is an object which we are able to trace as a movement of thought, a movement of memory reaching down into the past and a movement of aspiration, probing towards an unrealized, and perhaps unrealizable futurity. Through the study of these artefacts, we are able to grasp ‘mind' as an external (and eternal) disposition of public acts of objectification, and simultaneously as the evolving consciousness of a collectivity, transcending the individual cogito and the coordinates of any particular here and now.
